techniques.name: K-window interface automaton: exclusion of eventual period words for every number-like configuration
techniques.origin: N. Berzai, 'The centre column of Rule 30: excluded periods, decimation of the Duhamel class, and the front of the diagonal defects' (99 pp.), Part I, in GitHub nateberzai-svg/rule30-left-edge
techniques.date: Paper assembled 2026-09-16 and revised 2026-09-24, with citations added in October 2026; repo last pushed 2026-10-08 (d9cb3d57)
techniques.ai_involvement: Author footnote: 'Computational and editorial assistance from Claude (Anthropic); three parallel referee dialogues (Opus 5) contributed Part III.'
forms: Problem 1, one eventual-period word at a time
eventual periodicity of the trace of number-like configurations (Kopra's setting)
shift orbit / Morse–Hedlund (excluding specific periodic tails)
techniques.core_idea: Assume column 0 is eventually w^∞. Over-approximate the right half by its first K cells, with cell K+1 free. The reachable window sets then form a finite period graph G_w. If every recurrent SCC has #edges = #vertices, column 1 read at the zero letters of w (the 'unmasked interface') is eventually periodic. By l(n)=c(n+1)⊕(c(n)∨u(n)), column −1 is then eventually periodic too, and Jen/Kopra forbid two adjacent eventually periodic columns.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Directly portable. Each certificate is a finite graph check plus our Rule30Jen/Rule30MaskedJen theorems. The exclusions hold for all finite seeds and do not depend on the onset time, so they would replace and enlarge Rule30StripCertificateTable. Running the engine over all primitive words of period 8–20 would grow the excluded set mechanically.
techniques.obstacle: Word-by-word only, and it stops before period 2. Round 1 found no primitive word of period ≤7 certified at K≤12, including 01, 001, 011, 0111 and 0011. Berzai's own boundary theorem says the method fails at every K once L(w) contains a non-eventually-periodic interface, and L(01) has measured positive entropy. This matches our barrier B1 (every finite abstraction has a reachable lasso): a finite over-approximation of the right half certifies only words whose interface it forces to be eventually periodic. It passes the Rule-90 firewall, because the interface identity uses the OR and Jen needs a finite left edge.
techniques.artifacts: paper/RULE30_PAPER.tex, wolfram_number_note.tex and verify_claims_output.txt (repo license MPL-2.0). The certificate engine is described in the paper's last section. Our round-1 re-implementation is research/lit-oss/scripts/berzai_kwindow.py (scratch path in round1.json).

techniques.core_idea: Under a hypothesised periodic word, a window of cells (−6..6, or one-sided of width 8) with free outer cells evolves on a finite graph. Any infinite history ends in a cyclic SCC, and inside it every edge advances the BFS class by one modulo the period. If a neighbouring column is constant on each class, two adjacent columns are eventually periodic, and Theorem A (Jen with a clock) finishes the proof.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Kernel-decidable tables (placego uses decide +kernel) that fit our packed-Nat kernel-decide style. They are a second, independent engine next to the K-window method, useful for cross-certification. The q-uniform steps are short hand proofs that can be reproved.
techniques.obstacle: Same reach as the K-window method. By our JointBarrier, B1/B2 and the foundry's free-boundary result (a 5-cell free strip admits a non-eventually-periodic neighbour for every nonconstant word), strips cannot settle 01. cochon123's original uniform Lemma F was wrong, which shows that AI-written uniform steps need an independent second reading.

techniques.name: Quantitative Jen (Theorem A), the window principle (Theorem A′) and bounded zero runs beside periodic columns (Theorem B)
techniques.origin: ghywel/placego, Claude 'Local' with GPT second reads: PERIOD-TWO.md §2 and PROOFS.md entries 5–7. Lean probe tests/probes/lean/TheoremA.lean.
techniques.ai_involvement: Proposed by Claude (Local), second-read by GPT; the Lean probe was written by Local.
techniques.proved:
- Theorem A: if the leftmost black cell at time 0 is L cells left of column c, and columns c and c+1 are P-periodic on the time window [a,b], then b ≤ 2a+L+2P−1. Jen's theorem is the case b=∞.
- Theorem A′: a block of two adjacent columns recurs at time a′ only if its length is ≤ L+a′.
- Theorem B: if columns 0 and 1 are P-periodic (P≥2), no zero run of the forced left half is longer than 2P−2.
- Lemmas B1–B3, A‴, A⁗: left-diagonal periods are unbounded; a settled band has no white run longer than twice its period.
A limited literature search by the project found no earlier statement of A or A′. TheoremA.lean (theorem_A, no_two_periodic) is not rebuilt by us.
forms: Problem 1, two-column (Jen) form with explicit clocks
effective transient/period bounds for finite windows
techniques.core_idea: Periodicity of two adjacent columns propagates one column left per step by left-permutivity, losing one time step at the end of the window. It reaches the light-speed left edge, where a cell turns black for the first time, and so cannot survive.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Gives Jen a clock. In a hypothetical counterexample, the aperiodic 'kicks' of column 1 cannot thin out faster than geometrically. It can be combined with our kernel-checked T+P≥16359 (Rule30FactorWindow) to say how long column 1 can mimic periodicity. The proof is a few lines and easy to re-derive in our Lean.
techniques.obstacle: It uses only left-permutivity and the moving edge, so it holds verbatim for Rules 90, 150 and 210, whose single-seed centres are eventually periodic (our Rule30Realization barrier). It can never exclude a single periodic column on its own.
techniques.artifacts: TheoremA.lean (Mathlib; placego has no LICENSE). Proof texts are in proofs/05-theorem-a-*.md and 06-theorem-b-*.md.

techniques.name: Excluding zero-entropy column-1 interfaces beside a period-2 centre (Theorems E, E″, Corollary F, A⁗; the 'wheel' description)
techniques.origin: ghywel/placego, Claude Local and GPT (G131–G136): RULE30-PRIZE.md §8.57–8.59 and PROOFS.md entries 11–15
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude (Local) proofs, GPT extensions and second reads, all inside the project
techniques.proved:
- Theorem E: if column 1's visible bits beside a 0101 centre form a Sturmian sequence, the forced left half is never finite.
- Theorem E″: the same for codings of a rotation by r arc endpoints whenever infinitely many partial quotients exceed 2^(r+1), so almost every rotation is excluded.
- Corollary F: near-squares at unbounded periods are fatal. This covers period-doubling, Chacon and every substitution fixed point that starts with a double letter.
- Theorem A⁗: Thue–Morse and paperfolding are excluded for every left edge up to 15,868 cells.
- Structural description (computed, with certificates): the column 1 that real right halves produce beside 0101 is 'the wheel', an exact coding of rotation by 17/56, kicked by domain walls. After about 133–140 steps the kicks fall into four local classes (Propositions 13 and 14).
All are second-read inside the project; none is externally reviewed.
techniques.core_idea: Combinatorics on words. A finite forced left half needs column 1 to contain specific near-repetitions and returns. Sturmian sequences, rotation codings and near-square-rich substitutive words either lack them or force a nonzero cell far to the left.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Supplies lemmas for our Q01/CQ01 programme that exclude whole classes of free-bit streams. The rotation-plus-kicks picture says what a counterexample's interface must look like.
techniques.obstacle: Every excluded class has zero entropy. Real right halves give a column 1 of positive entropy (about 0.08 bits per visible bit, measured), so this does not reach the positive-entropy constrained system that our barrier analysis says remains.

techniques.name: Channel bound: certified entropy ceiling for column 1 beside a 0101 centre
techniques.origin: ghywel/placego, Claude Local: RULE30-PRIZE.md §8.20 and §8.33, summarised in PERIOD-TWO.md §2
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude (Local), with predictions committed before runs; GPT read the results
techniques.proved: For every layer width m, the visible column-1 words beside 0101 produced by a width-m layer with a free input form a regular language, and h(column 1) ≤ log2 λ_m. The bound falls to about 0.122 bits per visible bit at m=28 by power iteration; PERIOD-TWO.md quotes 0.1236 certified at m=28 and 0.1292 certified in integer arithmetic. m=1 gives the golden ratio, the no-11 language. The project states as a theorem that wider layers never raise the bound.
forms: 'every orbit of a positive-entropy constrained system eventually violates a constraint'
techniques.core_idea: Replace the right half by a finite layer with a free boundary input. The possible column-1 outputs form a sofic language, and the spectral radius of its automaton bounds how much information column 1 can deliver beside the wall.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This is the delivery side of a counting proof. Showing that keeping the 0101 wall costs more than about 0.124 bits per visible bit of column 1 would exclude period 2.
techniques.obstacle: An upper bound only. The matching cost side, a lower bound on the information the wall consumes, is exactly the open positive-entropy statement. As a strip method it falls under our strip and finite-abstraction barriers when used alone.

techniques.name: Counting form and the exact one-bit-per-step left payment
techniques.origin: ghywel/placego RULE30-PRIZE.md §8.51 and PERIOD-TWO.md §5 'the one missing statement' (Claude Local and Cloud, GPT)
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude (Local/Cloud) and GPT
techniques.proved:
Lemma (proved): split N_w(T) by the position j of column 0 inside a hull of width w. Then N_{w,j}(T) = N_{w,j}(1)/2^(T−1) exactly for 1≤T≤j, because x_t(0)=x_0(−t)⊕g_t and cell −t is free.
Measured: N_w(T) ≈ 2^(w−1.05T+c) for the word 0101, exact counts up to w=24 (about 2×10^8 pairs). The same slope holds for the constant words that Condrey's theorem closes and for random words.
Conjecture (counting form): N_w(T) ≤ 2^(w−αT+O(1)) for some α>0. This would exclude period 2, because a count below 1 is 0.
techniques.core_idea: Count the finite configurations whose column reads the word for T steps. While unused left cells remain, each step halves the count exactly. After that, every condition must be paid by right-half bits entering through column 1.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: States our remaining sentence as a number that can be measured and certified. It suggests a size argument in the style of Chebyshev and Bertrand rather than any randomness statement.
techniques.obstacle: The right-paid half is the open problem. The measured law also holds for random centre words, so a proof must use what is special about periodic words, as Jen and Condrey do. Measurements are calibration, not mechanism (placego §8.116).
techniques.artifacts: rule30_count.py and count.c in placego (not run by us; no LICENSE)

- Exact local language counts 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 17, 25, 36, 50, 68, 91, 119 for lengths 1–12, with 12 minimal forbidden factors: 11, 00000, 101001, 0100101, 010010001, 0101000101, 0101010000, 01010001001, 10010001001, 010010000101, 010100010001, 100100010000. These are DRAT-certified, and every allowed factor has a retained finite realising row.

techniques.core_idea: Reduce period 2 to the forced initial left half e_j = completion(u,N). Physical u lives in a constrained language with explicit forbidden factors. A finite counterexample needs some physical u whose forced left weight W_N stays bounded.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Port the 12 forbidden factors to Lean as kernel-checked right-half laws for CQ01. They strictly strengthen our 'no 11111' law (col1_black_among_five, which is no-00000 in their convention). The L4 conjecture '7·weight(completion_from_u(u,N)) ≥ N−8 for every u avoiding the 12 factors' is a crisp, SAT-falsifiable combinatorial target that would imply period-2 exclusion.

The L1–L3 ladder was refuted by u=(01)^45 000101 (deficit 9), and the L4 queries at N=191 and N=300 returned UNKNOWN. L4 is a relaxation and may be false even if period 2 holds. It escapes our Q01-only barriers because it uses right-half laws that truncated stripes violate. Any proof of it still has to beat B1-type lassos, since an SFT of u is a finite-memory abstraction.

techniques.name: Rule 210: period-2 exclusion by a clearing-front argument (Proposition 19), with LR false
techniques.origin: ghywel/placego, PROOFS.md entry 32 (clearing-front proof by GPT, GC478; second-read by hand by Claude Local, L285) and RULE30-PRIZE.md §8.65 / G26
techniques.ai_involvement: Proof by GPT, verified by hand by Claude (Local)
techniques.proved:
Rule 210 (x′ = l ⊕ (¬c ∧ r)) with centre clock t mod 2:
- Every finite initial-left row admits at most one full realisation. Odd-supported rows have exactly one, the parity-sparse realisation, and its right seed is infinite. Rows containing an even left site are excluded.
- Hence no finite Rule 210 seed keeps the 0101 clock.
- Conjecture LR is false for Rule 210. The column 1 with runs 1, 1, 2, 4, 8, … keeps the left half empty; on that sublattice the system is Rule 90 driven by 0101.
Rule 30 is the only remaining open sibling at period 2: Rule 90 also has no period-2 column (placego Proposition 5).
forms: Problem 1 at period 2 for the sibling rule
techniques.core_idea: Track adjacent diagonal pairs with a marker M_j=(1−P_j)Q_j. A clearing pulse followed by a 01 front propagates diagonal by diagonal. Matching the front to the parity background forces the right seed to be infinite.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: A two-sided template: a finite left row forces a unique realisation with an infinite right half. Because LR is false for 210 while finite-seed period 2 holds, our left-only Q01 may be strictly stronger than what Problem 1 needs. Our CQ01 (coupled) programme is the right shape.
techniques.obstacle: Transfer to Rule 30 is recorded as invalid. The analogous front statement holds trivially for Rule 30 (marker M=P OR Q, N30=4) and carries no information (SW-01 proposal 10; blockers GC479 and GC549). techniques.name: Duhamel formula (Rule 150 propagator plus quadratic source) and Cartier-operator closure of the 2-kernel
techniques.origin: N. Berzai, Part II of the rule30-left-edge paper. The same exact forcing identity F_t = L^t F_0 + Σ L^(t−1−s) Q_s is also in Patto1155/rule30-foundry.
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude (computation and editing) for Berzai; Codex and Claude agents for the foundry
techniques.proved:
PROVED:
- U_{t+1} = Λ U_t + Q_t, with Λ = z+1+z^(−1) and Q_t = Σ u_x u_{x+1} z^x. Hence c_t = 1 + Σ_{s<t} Σ_x T_{t−1−s}(x) u^s_x u^s_{x+1}, where T_m(0)=1.
- The class of such functionals is closed under the Cartier operators Λ_0 and Λ_1, so the 2-kernel of c is the image of an explicit orbit.
- The functional has a closed form in α, with y = α/(1+α+α²). Only the centre line and the chiral part of the source are visible to c.
- deg F_t = 2t−1, with a unique top monomial.
- Under the uniform measure, the two-point function of any left-permutive radius-1 rule vanishes off the ray x=t.
EXACT (certified): no Mahler relation of depth ≤12 and degree ≤8000; a 2-kernel census of ≥138,672 distinct truncations from 2^21 terms. The census route is closed: from 2^ν terms at most 2^(ν−4)−1 elements can be certified, and padded prefixes are automatic.
forms: non-rationality of Σ c(t)x^t over F_2
techniques.core_idea: Rule 30 is Rule 150 driven by the quadratic source Q (exactly the OR's nonlinearity). Because Λ(z)² = Λ(z²) in characteristic 2, decimating by 2 maps the Duhamel class to itself. This gives an explicit dynamical system on source data whose orbit is the 2-kernel, and non-automaticity is equivalent to that orbit being infinite.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30:
The most concrete algebraic handle on our F_2 power-series forms. Two possible routes:
- an invariant of the chiral Cartier recursion that takes infinitely many values;
- a family of residues meeting the Allouche–Shallit–Yassawi kernel criterion: one residue class per level, with pairwise-distinct kernel elements.
Either would make Σ c(t)x^t transcendental and give Problem 1.
techniques.obstacle: The target is strictly stronger than Problem 1 (Thue–Morse is automatic and aperiodic), and no such invariant is known. No finite census can decide it: every finite word extends to an automatic sequence. It is global and algebraic, so our local, strip and DFA barriers do not apply. It passes the Rule-90 firewall by construction, because the source vanishes for linear rules. It has produced no theorem yet.
techniques.artifacts: Berzai paper Part II sections: 'The Duhamel formula and the 2-kernel', 'Certified bounds', 'Decimation of the Duhamel class' (MPL-2.0). Working document rule30_automaticity.pdf is cited there (we do not hold it). Foundry CLAIM_LEDGER has the forcing identity (no LICENSE).

techniques.name: Lucas-basis support calculus and finite automaticity/algebraicity bounds
techniques.origin: T. Nersissian, arXiv 2609.25077 and 2609.25078, and the Zenodo series U1, U4, U5, U6 plus 18921456. D. Fomin proved the support identity and corrected the centre-column formula (Zenodo 22646809).
techniques.date: Nersissian Zenodo 18921456 2026-03-09; Zenodo U-series 2026-09-14; arXiv 2026-09-18 (v1); Fomin v6 2026-09-07
techniques.ai_involvement: Not stated in Nersissian's papers. Fomin's bundle contains multi-agent 'assault' workflow memos (workflow IDs wf_…), but the papers themselves state no AI use.
techniques.proved:
Nersissian:
- Newton supports satisfy S_m = Inc(S_{m−1} Δ S_{m−2} Δ (S_{m−1} ⊛ S_{m−2})), where ⊛ is OR-convolution.
- min S_m = ⌊m/2⌋ and max S_m ≤ F_{m+1}−1.
- The right-diagonal least period is 2^⌈log2(max S_m+1)⌉ ≥ ⌊m/2⌋+1, so it is unbounded.
- Left record periods satisfy Q_m ≥ ½ log2(m+2).
- In the integer lift, deg D_k = F_{k+2}−1.
- U5: any 2-DFAO generating c needs ≥8,191 states reading least-significant digit first, and ≥12,950 reading most-significant first. A full-rank coefficient matrix excludes algebraic equations inside stated degree–height bounds.
- U4: each fixed integer layer has a D-finite space–time series and a P-recursive central column.
Fomin: proves the support identity d_m = L_{S_m} and c(t) = #{r ∈ S_{t+1} : r ⊆ t} mod 2. He refutes the identity c(t) = [t ∈ S_{t+1}] of arXiv 2604.00165 (agreement 21/35).
Round 1 checked Nersissian's support facts numerically for m≤24.
forms: automatic / Christol strengthening (finite state lower bounds)
algebraicity of Σ c(t)x^t over F_2 (finite exclusions)
techniques.core_idea: Lift the diagonals from F_2 to Z in the binomial (Lucas) basis. XOR becomes symmetric difference, AND becomes OR-convolution of supports, and discrete integration becomes a +1 shift. The centre column becomes a parity of supports filtered by bitwise containment r ⊆ t.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: An exact formula for c(t) in terms of supports. It is a candidate source for the 'unbounded family of distinguishable continuations' that Nersissian names as what non-automaticity needs. The integer layers connect to our planned Fatou/Pólya–Carlson form over Q.
techniques.obstacle: Every centre-column statement is finite (state bounds, degree–height rectangles). Fomin shows the Lucas transform is an involution and that windows are pure transients, so evaluation has no shortcut. Diagonal-period unboundedness also holds for Rule 90's Pascal diagonals, whose centre is 1,0,0,…, so diagonal facts alone cannot give Problem 1.

techniques.name: Support-wave anatomy: automaton-generated front, odometer crest, pure-transient windows and the single-orbit discrepancy reduction
techniques.origin: D. Fomin, 'The support wave of Rule 30' with companion papers 'Local grammars…' and 'Odometer and vacuum', Zenodo 22646809 (v6)
techniques.ai_involvement: The bundle includes memos of two multi-agent 'proof assaults' in Russian (workflow wf_6d7a64b0-4c8, ten lenses at maximum effort). Their claims are labelled as not adversarially checked.
techniques.proved:
Hand proofs plus scripts:
- The front moves at speed exactly 1/2, and the co-moving boundary layer is generated by an explicit finite automaton Φ (period 2B measured for B=2..2048).
- The tail run of row 2^n equals #{m : max S_m < 2^n}, characterising OEIS A094604 as odometer carries.
- Every window [0,2^k) evolves as a pure transient of length 2^(k+1)+1, with an empty fixed point.
- Coin lemma: at doubling levels the phase bit is a fair coin. A peeling theorem and an anti-shift conjugacy also hold.
- Reduction: the zero-column halving, the convergence of diagonal word frequencies and the centre density each reduce to a square-root discrepancy statement for one deterministic orbit.
techniques.core_idea: The left flank's supports form a wave with two provably regular skins: an automaton front and an odometer crest. Everything rigid is exhausted by coin digits and conjugations, and what remains is an exponential-sum bound for a single orbit.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Points to digit-discrepancy and exponential-sum technology (Mauduit–Rivat type) rather than dynamics for the density and normality forms.
techniques.obstacle: All rigid statements concern the regular flank. The centre column reads the wave 'between its two provably regular skins', where neither applies. The work says nothing about periodicity of c.

techniques.proved:
Condrey:
- Lemma 1, triangular uniqueness: the same right half and the same centre trace force equal configurations.
- Theorem 2: the zero-trace fibre, in prefix-OR form.
- Theorem 3: the all-one fibre has a universal checkerboard left half.

techniques.name: Problem-3 and complexity-measure obstructions with controls: A5 window monoid, rank route, Rule 126 as the Fredholm–Rueppel sequence
techniques.origin: N. Berzai, Part V and the closed-routes table of the rule30-left-edge paper
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude (computational and editorial assistance)
techniques.proved:
- The window transformation monoid of Rule 30 contains A5, so it is not solvable; this places the rule on the hard side of the Barrington–Thérien and Moore dichotomies.

surveys.notes:
BOTTOM LINE (checked 2026-10-15)
No 2024–2026 project has excluded any nonconstant eventual period of the single-seed centre column, whether AI-assisted or not.

Period 1 is settled for every nonzero finite configuration. Condrey proved it (arXiv 2609.09431, Claude Opus 5 assisted), and as of today it is formalised in core Lean 4.19 on the rule30-foundry branch research/period2-column-ladder. That branch has no license and we did not rebuild it.

Every serious project converges on the same wall, worded differently:
- placego: 'no emptiness from a constrained side of positive entropy';
- foundry: no transport bound from local u-language bans to unbounded left weight;
- Berzai: an uncountable interface language L(01) defeats every K;
- Fomin: a single-orbit discrepancy problem.
This is our barrier statement. The wall is now independently confirmed by five groups and several model families: Claude, GPT, Codex, Kimi and DeepSeek.

techniques.name: Elementary non-holonomy engine plus Stanley's theorem in Lean (a P-recursive sequence with finitely many values is eventually periodic)
techniques.origin: Ralf Stephan (independent, IGDORE), Lean 4 written 'in collaboration with Claude Code' (file headers). Repository rwst/Ceiling-Orbits; paper 'Ceiling orbits of rational bases are not P-recursive' (ResearchGate DOI 10.13140/RG.2.2.10727.82081). Classical inputs: Stanley, Eur. J. Combin. 1 (1980), Thm 2.1 and half of Thm 1.5.
techniques.date: Repo created 2026-07-29, last push 2026-09-07. Stanley's closure property changed from cited axiom to proved theorem on 2026-09-06 (Challenge.lean docstring).
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude Code (Anthropic) produced the Lean under the author's direction and review. The mathematics is elementary or classical; the AI contribution is the formalization.
techniques.proved: RB.eventuallyPeriodic_of_isPRecursive: if w : N -> Q has finite range and satisfies a nontrivial recurrence sum_j Q_j(n) w(n+j) = 0 with Q_j in Q[t], then w is eventually periodic. The proof uses no analysis and depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound (std3). The library also has the contrapositive (RB.not_isPRecursive_of_not_eventuallyPeriodic); eventuallyPeriodic_of_rational_of_finite_coeffs; and eventuallyPeriodic_of_isAlgebraic_of_finite_coeffs (algebraic over Q(z) plus finitely many coefficient values gives eventual periodicity). Stanley.pRecursive_of_isAlgebraic is proved in CITED/StanleyProof.lean over any field of characteristic 0. Applied there: for every rational base p/q, the ceiling-orbit word is not P-recursive and its series is transcendental over Q(z). The comparator config permits only std3 axioms.
forms: non-rationality of sum c(t) z^t over Q (Fatou/Polya-Carlson family)
non-holonomy (not P-recursive) and transcendence of sum c(t) z^t over Q(z)
techniques.core_idea: Pigeonhole on windows: past some N, every length-(s+1) window recurs infinitely often. So sum_j Q_j(t) w(m+j) is a polynomial in t with infinitely many roots, and its top-degree coefficients give a constant-coefficient recurrence. A constant-coefficient recurrence on a finite alphabet makes the window evolve deterministically on a finite set, so the word is eventually periodic. Stanley's step: K(X)(f) is a finite extension closed under d/dX, so f, f', ..., f^(d) are linearly dependent over K(X). That gives an ODE and then a P-recursion.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Directly reusable in the equivalents library: Problem 1 iff the center column (as N -> Q) is not P-recursive, iff sum c(t) z^t in Q[[z]] is not algebraic over Q(z), iff it is not rational over Q. All three come with an elementary proof and need neither Fatou nor Polya-Carlson. This also settles, as a theorem, why holonomic methods (Apery-type, conservative matrix fields, G-functions, holonomy bounds) can never work on f itself: f is D-finite exactly when Problem 1 fails.
techniques.obstacle: These are equivalences and give no leverage for a proof. Only the natural-boundary form still needs Szego/Polya-Carlson analysis, which I found formalized nowhere. Porting: the repo uses toolchain v4.33.0-rc1, the library v4.30.0. The pinned Mathlib (c5ea003) lacks PowerSeries.coeff_iterate_derivative, but has the DifferentialAlgebra instance for finite intermediate fields that Stanley's step relies on (Mathlib/FieldTheory/Differential/Basic.lean:190). There is no barrier conflict, because nothing about rule 30 is used.
techniques.artifacts: CC0 Lean: RB/EventuallyPeriodic.lean (~24 KB, the engine); CITED/StanleyProof.lean (~28 KB: fracDeriv by the dual-numbers trick, exists_ode, coefficient-recurrence extraction); CITED/Stanley.lean. Challenge.lean defines Stanley.IsPRecursive against Mathlib only. Read here, not built.

techniques.name: Kronecker-Hankel rationality criterion and 2-adic digit periodicity in Lean
techniques.origin: Ralf Stephan with Claude Code, repo rwst/Transcendence-Criteria: ForMathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/{Rationality,EventuallyPeriodic}.lean, B3/DigitPeriodicity.lean, BL/Basic.lean. Classical sources: Kronecker; Bertin et al., 'Pisot and Salem Numbers' (1992), Prop. 1.1; Lagarias, Acta Arith. 56 (1990).
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude Code wrote the Lean ('(C) 2026 Ralf Stephan, in collaboration with Claude Code'). The mathematics is classical.
techniques.proved: isRationalSeries_iff_kroneckerDet_eventually_zero: over an integral domain, a power series is rational iff its Hankel (Kronecker) determinants vanish for all large n. isRationalSeries_iff_isEventuallyPeriodic_coeff: when the coefficients take finitely many values, rational iff eventually periodic. B3.not_isEventuallyPeriodic_binaryDigit and B3.ratInt_eventuallyPeriodic_binaryDigit: the 2-adic digits of v in Z_2 are eventually periodic iff v is in Q.
forms: non-rationality over F2 and over Q
techniques.core_idea: Kronecker: a singular Hankel matrix has a kernel vector, which gives a recurrence. A block-determinant identity, q0^(t+1) D_t = +- q0^s D_(s-1) v^(t-s+1), then propagates the recurrence once D_(s-1) != 0 and D_n = 0 for n >= s. 2-adic: a purely p-periodic digit block gives (1 - 2^p) w = C in Z_2, so w = C/(1 - 2^p) is rational. Conversely, a rational 2-adic integer has a finite shift orbit.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Two new catalogue entries. First, Problem 1 iff sum c(t) 2^t in Z_2 is irrational. Second, Problem 1 iff det[c(i+j)] for 0 <= i, j <= n is nonzero for infinitely many n, over ZMod 2 or over Z. Over F2 this is a determinant restatement of the unbounded linear complexity the library already has.
techniques.obstacle: These are equivalences only. When porting, do not import BL/ConjugacyMap.lean: it declares unrelated axioms (Phi_eq_neg_sum, Phi_image_ratInt_subset, nowhere-differentiability). Likewise AB/StammeringSequences.lean declares the axiom isStammering_of_automatic. DigitPeriodicity.lean imports both chains, so run #print axioms after porting; I did not confirm its footprint.
techniques.artifacts: CC0 Lean: Rationality.lean (~34 KB, with kroneckerDet_step); EventuallyPeriodic.lean (~11 KB); ForMathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/{Hankel,Determinant/AntiDiagonal}.lean; B3/DigitPeriodicity.lean (~5 KB). Toolchain v4.33.0-rc1.

techniques.name: Window-residue rigidity plus growth ceiling for rational-base words (aperiodicity of the 3/2 minimal word and of every p/q ceiling orbit)
techniques.origin: Ralf Stephan, Lean with Claude Code. Classical results it formalizes: Akiyama-Frougny-Sakarovitch, Israel J. Math. 168 (2008), Prop. 26; Dubickas, Glasgow Math. J. 51 (2009), Thm 2. Context for rule 30: J. Kopra, 'Rapid left expansivity...', TCS 946 (2023) 113668, arXiv 2202.13809.
techniques.date: arXiv 2609.19007 v1 2026-07-18, v2 2026-09-17. Transcendence-Criteria repo 2026-07-18 to 2026-08-06. Ceiling-Orbits repo, which generalizes to every p/q, 2026-07-29 to 2026-09-07.
techniques.ai_involvement: The paper's Acknowledgements say the author 'utilized Claude Code as an AI coding assistant to aid in the Lean 4 formalization'. The aperiodicity mathematics is classical.
techniques.proved:
For x_(n+1) = ceil(3 x_n / 2) and w_n = x_n mod 2:
(i) Windows of length m agree at a and b iff 2^m divides x_b - x_a (RB.isRepetition_iff_dvd).
(ii) A repeated length-k window at a < c forces 2^(k+c) < 3^c (x0 + 1); at x0 = 1 this is 41k <= 24c + 40.
(iii) w is not eventually periodic (RB.not_eventually_periodic, std3), and its complexity satisfies P(w, m) >= floor(41(m-1)/24) + 1.
Ceiling-Orbits proves the same for every coprime p > q >= 2. Note that the irrationality of K(3) = 1.6222705... stays open: in base 3/2, aperiodic digits do not imply irrationality.
forms: eventual periodicity of a digit word (Problem 1 shape)
techniques.core_idea: The integer state x_n consumes one binary digit per step, and the inverse step is a 2-adic contraction. So a length-m window of the word pins x_n modulo 2^m. A repetition therefore costs a factor 2^k in |x_c - x_a|, while the state grows only like (3/2)^c. Because log2(3/2) < 1, long repetitions, and with them eventual periodicity, are impossible.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: The exact rule-30 analog already exists: it is the Jen-Kopra width-2 theorem. Left-permutivity, old(i-1) = new(i) XOR (old(i) OR old(i+1)), makes a window of two adjacent columns over [T, T+m] determine the row at time T on [-m, 1]; that is the window-residue rigidity. The left light-cone edge (cell(t, -t) = 1, zero beyond) is the ceiling. If two adjacent columns were periodic, the rows at T and T+P would agree on all of [-m, 1] for every m, which contradicts the moving edge. To reach width 1 (Problem 1) one needs an extra relation that pins a neighbouring column from the center column. Condrey's defect identity supplies one only on {t : c(t) = 1}.
techniques.obstacle: One column does not determine the left half, because the right half is free. The state behind the center column therefore gains at least one free bit per step while each digit pins one bit: there is no entropy deficit like log2(3/2) < 1. Rules 90, 150 and 210 are left-permutive with the same light cone and have eventually constant centers (Rule30Realization.barrier; Kopra's own remark). Any width-1 rigidity must therefore use the OR nonlinearity. The argument does not conflict with the strip, finite-state or additive barriers, but it does not get past them either.
techniques.artifacts: CC0 Lean (v4.33.0-rc1): RB/Rigidity.lean; RB/GeneralBase.lean (general p/q); ForMathlib/Combinatorics/SubwordComplexity.lean, a finite Morse-Hedlund (complexity <= n on a window of length >= 3n forces a long periodic factor) that is useful for window certificates like Rule30FactorWindow; ForMathlib/Combinatorics/InfiniteComplexity.lean (left-special factors of every length). Comparator configs come with it. Read here, not built.

techniques.name: Block (confinement) certificates for Mahler-type sets Z_(p/q)(s, s+t), checked by the Lean kernel
techniques.origin: Ralf Stephan with Claude Code; repo rwst/Confinement-Certificates; papers 'Confinement certificates for powers of rational numbers modulo one' plus a 'schemas' companion (ResearchGate 411967777). Builds on Flatto-Lagarias-Pollington and on Dubickas-Novikas.
techniques.date: Repo created 2026-08-08, last push 2026-09-12. Toolchain v4.34.0-rc2; 40 Lean files, ~850 KB.
techniques.ai_involvement: The Lean is 'in collaboration with Claude Code' (file headers), human-directed. No other AI is credited.
techniques.proved:
Per the README abstract:
- Z_(3/2)(1/6, 13/24) is empty (window length 3/8 > 1/3) and Z_(3/2)(961/3600, 2427/3600) is empty.
- Unions of windows of total length up to 17/24 are empty, against 20/39 in print.
- No xi != 0 keeps ||xi (3/2)^n|| < 1/5 for all n.
- FLP Cor. 1.4a and Dubickas's theorem for 1 < q < p < q^2 are formalized in full.
- Thirty length-1/p windows at five bases with p > q^2 are certified.
The README says everything is std3, with no native code.
forms: constrained-orbit form ('every orbit eventually violates a constraint', the shape of Q01 and Absorption)
techniques.core_idea: Finite integer witnesses, re-checked by the kernel's own evaluator, show that any orbit confined to the window has an eventually periodic integer-part word. An independent aperiodicity lemma (Dubickas-Novikas) then rules that out. So the 'lasso' that any finite abstraction contains is harmless: its realization is killed by the lemma.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This pattern answers 'finite abstraction has a lasso' (Rule30ZeroBoundaryBarriers.finite_abstraction_has_lasso): a lasso is acceptable if every run that stays in it forces an eventually periodic column, and an aperiodicity lemma kills that column. Rule 30 does have such lemmas: Rule30DrivenLeft.no_periodic_column (Jen; a periodic driver makes no left column eventually periodic), Kopra's width-2 theorem, and Condrey's no-constant-column result. A certificate for Q01 or Absorption would have to show that every constrained infinite run of the abstraction forces some left column to be eventually periodic.
techniques.obstacle: That is possible only when the constrained abstraction's reachable strongly connected components are single cycles, i.e. zero entropy. The Q01 and Absorption systems have positive entropy, and no local or edge-DFA ranking exists for them (no_local_ranking, no_edge_dfa_ranking). So the method can at best close more bounded-width cases, like the existing width-52/56 certificates, not the general statement. Cost data: the largest certificate's kernel check takes ~100 s and 12 GB.
techniques.artifacts: CC0 Lean with a kernel-evaluated certificate checker (Z32.BlockCert) and comparator configs. Read here, not built.

techniques.name: 2-adic valuation trap (Lagarias: divergent 3x+1 trajectories have aperiodic parity sequences), formalized with Claude Code
techniques.origin: J. C. Lagarias, Acta Arith. 56 (1990), Cor. 2.1b; Lean by Ralf Stephan with Claude Code (rwst/Transcendence-Criteria, L90/DivergentAperiodic.lean, L90/RationalCycles.lean).
techniques.date: Lean 2026-07/08 (repo 2026-07-18 to 2026-08-06); the mathematics is from 1990.
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude Code formalization. Per the docstring, the realization result L90.xCycle_realizes went from cited axiom to proved theorem.
techniques.proved: An eventually periodic parity sequence forces a finite orbit (not_divergent_of_eventuallyPeriodicParity), for all x in Q intersect Z_2. The docstring says the file is sorry-free and std3.
techniques.core_idea: Over one period of the parity block, the dynamics is an affine map 2^n T^n(x) = 3^c x + S. Differences of consecutive period-returns satisfy 2^(nk) d_k = 3^(ck) d_0. Odd denominators then force 2^(nk) to divide the numerator of d_0 for every k, so d_0 = 0 and the orbit is periodic.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: The natural rule-30 home is the leftward spatial recursion A_(i-1) = S(A_i) + A_i + A_(i+1) + A_i (.) A_(i+1) over F2[[x]], where A_i(x) = sum_t cell(t, i) x^t, S is the time shift and (.) is the Hadamard product. The zero boundary is a valuation-growth condition, ord_x A_(-k) >= k. A trap would show that a periodic A_0 forces the stable set of this expanding map to be a single 'rational' point that is incompatible with the light-cone edge.
techniques.obstacle: Rule 30's row map is not affine over Z (XOR has no carries, and OR is nonlinear). The right-half diagonal dynamics is a 2-adic isometry, an odometer (Coven-Pivato-Yassawi; research/verify-B-odometer-rigor), not a contraction. Rule 90 has the same expanding shift structure without the (.) term, and its periodic-center solution exists. So any trap must exploit the Hadamard (OR) term, and no such argument is known.
techniques.artifacts: CC0 Lean: L90/DivergentAperiodic.lean (~16 KB), L90/RationalCycles.lean (~25 KB), BL/Basic.lean (2-adic shift S and parity on Z_2).

techniques.name: Tail-decay (Liouville / Erdos-Straus) irrationality for rapidly converging series: AI-era instances Erdos #1051 and #258
techniques.origin: #1051: Aletheia, Google DeepMind's agent built on Gemini Deep Think (Feng et al.); generalized by Barreto, Kang, Kim, Kovac and Zhang; Lean by K. Barreto, by ByteDance Seed-Prover 1.5, and in LeanMarathon (Zhang, Sun, Suzuki, Lee, Liu). #258: P. Chojecki with GPT-5.4 Pro (erdosproblems.com; Tao-Teravainen's Remark 1.4 says GPT 5.4 Thinking), via Tao-Teravainen Thm 1.1.
techniques.date: Aletheia's solution came in December 2025 and was made public 2026-01-29/30. BKKKZ arXiv v1 2026-01-29, v3 2026-07-08 (accepted, Bull. LMS). Seed-Prover's erdos_1051.lean was in the repo by its 2026-02-13 push. LeanMarathon arXiv 2026-06-03. #258 note dated 2026-04-14; problem page edited 2026-05-28.
techniques.ai_involvement: Aletheia autonomously solved the original #1051. Four of five human graders accepted its output; one objected to an unjustified 'standard comparison theorems' step (arXiv 2601.22401). Gemini Deep Think found a generalization. Humans proved the golden-ratio threshold and the counterexamples and wrote the paper. Seed2.0 re-derived the proof, and Seed-Prover 1.5 formalized it. For #258, GPT-5.4 noticed that an existing theorem settles the problem and wrote the 2-page note.
techniques.proved: #1051: if a_n is strictly increasing with limsup a_n^(1/phi^n) = infinity, then sum 1/(a_n a_(n+1)) is irrational. The threshold is sharp: rational examples exist with a_n^(1/phi^n) -> C for any C > 1. There is a d-term generalization. #258: sum tau(n)/(a_1 ... a_n) is irrational whenever a_n -> infinity, the Erdos-Straus conjecture.
techniques.core_idea: If S = P/Q, then Q D_N (S - S_N) is a positive integer for every N, where D_N clears the denominators of the first N terms. Fast growth makes this integer < 1 along a subsequence; for #258 the input is infinitely many N with tau(N+k) <= Lambda^k. The golden ratio is where the denominator exponent and the tail exponent balance.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: For x = sum c(t) 2^(-t-1) the lemma reads: if x = a/q then frac(2^N x) is in (1/q)Z, so every white run that is followed by a black cell is shorter than log2 q + 1. Hence 'c has arbitrarily long white runs' (or black runs, via the complement) is a sufficient condition for Problem 1. It is strictly stronger than Problem 1 and of Problem-2 type. Empirically, the run records grow like log2 n: white 22 (at 5,241,994) and black 23 (at 1,174,512) within the first 10^7 bits (my scripts/runs.py, checked against direct simulation).
techniques.obstacle: Binary digits decay exactly geometrically, which matches the denominator 2^N, so there is no Liouville slack. The only handle left is a rare-pattern statement about one deterministic orbit, and no tool produces those. Rule30BlackRuns' Theorem B bounds black runs only inside a hypothetical period, not in c itself.
techniques.artifacts: erdos_1051.lean (141 KB, Apache-2.0); LeanMarathon (Apache-2.0); formal-conjectures statements 1051.lean and 258.lean (Apache-2.0); the ulam.ai note.

techniques.name: Conspiracy repulsion: rationality congruences plus dilation identities plus two-point correlation estimates (Tao-Teravainen)
techniques.origin: Terence Tao and Joni Teravainen, 'Quantitative correlations and some problems on prime factors of consecutive integers'. The phrase 'conspiracy repulsion' is from Tao's comment on V. Kovac's erdosproblems.com blog post 'Paul Erdos and irrationality problems for series'.
techniques.date: arXiv v1 2025-12-01, v2 2026-04-25. Blog post and Tao's comment 2026-02-02. Problem pages #69 and #257 last edited 2026-04-15.
techniques.ai_involvement: None in the proof: 'the text in this paper is entirely human-generated'; ChatGPT generated plotting code. Tao used Gemini 3 Pro to locate the Siegel-Shidlovsky theorem for a toy series on the blog (2026-02-02). OpenAI's 2026-10-06 release claims, without independent check, the ordinary two-point Chowla and corrected binary Elliott conjectures (family 007). Those are inputs of this type.
techniques.proved: sum omega(n)/2^n is irrational, and so is the Omega version in any base b >= 2. This settles Erdos #69 and the prime and prime-power cases of #257. Also: infinitely many n with omega(n+k) <= Omega(n+k) << k for all k.
techniques.core_idea: Rationality a/q gives q sum_h omega(n+h)/2^h = 0 (mod 1) for every shift n. Additivity under dilation, omega(pn) = omega(n) + 1 - 1_(p|n), transports this congruence to dilated shifts. A Gowers-cube alternating sum over primes p_eps = p_0 + eps.v cancels the first K terms. Taking expectations over a random n, the resulting combination must be ~ 0 mod 1, yet correlation estimates (after Pilatte) make it spread out: contradiction.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This would need (i) an exact dilation or self-similarity identity for c and (ii) quantitative two-point decorrelation of c at every shift h. Condition (ii) alone already implies Problem 1: a period h forces correlation 1 at h. So a 'Chowla conjecture for the rule-30 center column' is a natural stronger target, sitting between Problems 1 and 2.
techniques.obstacle: Rule 30 has neither ingredient. The barrier theorems bite: rule 90 has the Frobenius dilation identity, cell(2t, 2i) = cell(t, i), and its center is eventually constant. So the structural ingredient points the wrong way, and the correlation input is Problem-2 hard.
techniques.artifacts: None reusable. formal-conjectures has the statements 69.lean and 257.lean (Apache-2.0).

techniques.proved: There exist integers g_n >= 2 with g_n = o(p_n) and sum p_n/(g_1 ... g_n) = 1. The construction picks c_(n+1) = -p_n (mod c_n) and lets the series telescope; I read the 1-page proof and found no gap. #263(ii): a negative answer, via concatenated blocks of consecutive integers. These models are good at generating such constructions quickly. Use them to stress-test every proposed lemma against synthetic 'periodic-center' models before attempting a proof.

techniques.name: AI-agent Erdos irrationality programmes with equivalence reformulations and finite exclusion certificates (Plectis)

techniques.proved:
Claims, each with a Lean-checked statement:
- #257: a weighted finite-prime-support irrationality theorem at every integer base; not every infinite support.
- #68: irrationality is equivalent to cofinally many non-unit factorial carries; any rational value must have denominator q >= 2^39990.
- #1049: irrationality in Zudilin's rational-base contour region, plus exact Hankel orders.
- #249: classification of totient-residue series at dyadic moduli.
- #269: transcendence via a cited Hecke-Mahler theorem.
All eight target problems remain open, apart from a refutation of a misformalized statement of #1041.
forms: finite exclusion of small periods / denominators
techniques.core_idea: Reformulate irrationality as an equivalent 'cofinally often' statement, exclude small denominators by finite certificates, and record conditional routes. Every claim is bound to a Lean declaration by Comparator; 87% of the 164,639 declarations are machine-emitted certificate shards.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This mirrors the Rule 30 program closely: equivalence library, plus finite exclusions such as T + P >= 16359 and the period <= 4096 bounds, plus conditional reductions. Its infrastructure (Comparator challenges, claim registry, Palomar registration) is a template for publishing the catalogue. #68's 'irrationality iff cofinal carries' is the same kind of statement as the library's.
techniques.obstacle: None of its mathematics concerns cellular automata. Its finite certificates exclude bounded denominators only, exactly like Rule30Window, and say nothing about the unbounded case.

techniques.name: Mahler's method (Adamczewski-Faverjon) and its partial Lean formalization
techniques.origin: B. Adamczewski and C. Faverjon, 'Mahler's method in several variables and finite automata' (Annals of Mathematics; arXiv 2012.08283) and Addendum (arXiv 2407.18578); [AF17] Proc. LMS 115 (2017). Lean: Ralf Stephan with Claude Code, 29 files CITED/AdamczewskiFaverjon*.lean.
techniques.ai_involvement: The method is human work. The Lean formalization was AI-assisted (Claude Code).
techniques.proved: AF: no irrational real number is automatic in two multiplicatively independent bases; a multivariate Nishioka theorem. In Lean, AF.transcendental_or_rat_of_automatic (AF17 Cor. 1.8 specialized) is a theorem modulo two cited axioms, AF.lemme_2_2 and AF.lemma_2_8: for automatic bounded a_j and rational alpha with 0 < |alpha| < 1, sum a_j alpha^j is transcendental or rational. Cobham's linear-complexity bound for automatic sequences is proved outright (AS.complexity_linear_of_automatic).
forms: Christol / non-automaticity / transcendence of the binary number
techniques.core_idea: The generating function of an automatic sequence satisfies a Mahler equation f(z^k) = R(z, f(z)). Algebraic relations among such values at algebraic points lift to functional relations (Nishioka, Philippon, AF). So the value is transcendental unless a functional relation forces it rational.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Only conditional and in the wrong direction: if c were 2-automatic, x would be rational or transcendental. Problem 1 is exactly the rational-versus-irrational question this dichotomy leaves open. The useful chain is the strengthening 'p_c superlinear => c not automatic (Cobham, proved in Lean) => sum c(t) x^t transcendental over F2(x) (Christol)', which is harder than Problem 1 (Nersissian's 8191-state certificate is only evidence).
techniques.obstacle: A dichotomy carries no information about the rational branch. It also needs a Mahler equation, which c (conjecturally) lacks. Christol's theorem itself is formalized nowhere I could find.
techniques.artifacts: CC0 Lean: CITED/AdamczewskiFaverjon*.lean (~0.6 MB); CITED/AlloucheShallit{Basic,Complexity}.lean (k-kernel automaticity; Cobham's bound, proved).

techniques.name: Adamczewski-Bugeaud stammering sequences and Subspace-Theorem complexity dichotomies (rational base 3/2), with Lean scaffolding
techniques.origin: Adamczewski and Bugeaud, Annals 165 (2007), Section 4 (Condition (*)_w). Lean and new rational-base theorems by Ralf Stephan with Claude Code: arXiv 2609.19007, Theorems B and C; arXiv 2607.11648, superlinear complexity of the (3/2)^n steering word; repos Superlinear-Complexity and Subspace-Theorems.
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude Code for the Lean. The formalization found that Theorem 1.3(i) of Nair-Kumar-Rout (arXiv 2506.02898) is false as printed, and refuted it in Lean (NKR.thm13i_unrepaired_false).
techniques.proved: In base 3/2: (B) if w is automatic, K is transcendental; (C) either the complexity of w is superlinear or K is irrational. The steering word of (3/2)^n has superlinear complexity. These hold modulo the Evertse-Schlickewei Subspace Theorem (axiom) and, for (B), two AF lemmas. In Lean, AB07's Condition (*)_w is formalized, with 'automatic => stammering' as a cited axiom. Subspace-Theorems has its arithmetic-heights layers landed; Roth and the Subspace Theorem are not yet proved.
techniques.core_idea: Repetitions near the start of the digit word give unusually good rational or S-unit approximations. The Subspace Theorem allows only finitely many such approximations. So the number is transcendental, or rational, or the word has superlinear complexity.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: In integer base 2 with digits {0,1}, rational iff eventually periodic, which the library already proves (BinaryIrrational.lean). The 'rational branch' therefore collapses to Morse-Hedlund, p(n) >= n + 1, which the library also has. Transcendence of x (AB07: an irrational algebraic number has p(n)/n -> infinity) is a strengthening, not a route.
techniques.obstacle: Vacuous for Problem 1. These methods only separate irrational algebraic from transcendental, or apply in non-integer bases where aperiodic digits can still give a rational value.
techniques.artifacts: AB/*.lean, CITED/SubspaceTheorem.lean (axiom) and CITED/Ridout.lean (CC0); Subspace-Theorems (Apache-2.0, Tau Ceti conventions).

techniques.name: Arithmetic holonomy bounds (Calegari-Dimitrov-Tang), including the 2-adic zeta(5) programme
techniques.origin: F. Calegari, V. Dimitrov, Y. Tang, 'The linear independence of 1, zeta(2), and L(2, chi_-3)', 218 pp.; 'Arithmetic holonomy bounds and effective Diophantine approximation' (ICM 2026 proceedings); talks on the irrationality of the 2-adic zeta_2(5).
techniques.ai_involvement: None (human work). The lean-eval AI-formalization leaderboard lists the CDT statements as an open target (sorry).
techniques.proved: L(2, chi_-3) is irrational, and 1, zeta(2), L(2, chi_-3) are linearly independent over Q. The ICM paper sketches effective irrationality measures (including for L(2, chi_-3) and the 2-adic zeta(5)) and a new proof that pi is transcendental. Irrationality of the 2-adic zeta_2(5) is announced in talks.
forms: non-rationality over Q / natural boundary (Polya-Carlson, Szego)
techniques.core_idea: This is a quantitative rationality and holonomicity criterion in the Borel-Dwork-Polya-Bertrandias-Andre line. Integer-coefficient power series that extend holomorphically, with controlled singularities, to a domain of conformal size > 1 form a space of bounded dimension. Applied to explicit Apery- or Zagier-type constructions, the target constant cannot be rational.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: None. For f(z) = sum c(t) z^t, Szego and Polya-Carlson say f is rational or has |z| = 1 as a natural boundary. The unit disc has conformal size exactly 1, the threshold, and f extends past it iff Problem 1 fails. The method needs auxiliary functions built from c that extend beyond conformal size 1; none is known, and f itself is D-finite only if c is periodic (entry 1).
techniques.obstacle: c has no analytic structure, and nothing in the method is specific to cellular automata. No 2024-2026 progress on Polya-Carlson-type natural-boundary criteria surfaced; the latest general criterion found is Bell-Gunn-Nguyen-Saunders, arXiv 2206.00862 (2022).
techniques.artifacts: None reusable. The lean-eval problem file has the statement only.

techniques.name: Determinant strategy for Catalan's constant (OpenAI internal model, with a 16 MB Lean development)
techniques.origin: OpenAI, unreleased internal model, family 005 of the github.com/openai/math release (719 manuscripts in 372 families). Third-party follow-up: S. Litsey, Lean bound mu(G) <= 1281 built on OpenAI's development. A competing human claim by Z.-W. Sun has a gap.
techniques.date: Manuscript dated 2026-09-24; release 2026-10-06. History: on 2026-10-07 three unrelated manuscripts were withdrawn for a sign error. Litsey repo 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-15. Sun: arXiv 2609.04176, 2026-09-03; Wachs's gap analysis arXiv 2609.22339, 2026-09-16.
techniques.ai_involvement: The proof and the Lean are model-produced. Per the README, results took on average ~3 hours of ChatGPT Pro compute each, and about 4,000 problems were posed.
techniques.proved: Claimed: Catalan's constant G = beta(2) = L(2, chi_-4) is irrational. Lean: ComparatorChallenges/Catalan.lean states Irrational (sum' j, (-1)^j / (2j+1)^2), with solution module OAI.NumberTheory.Catalan.Main (981 files, ~16 MB). The config permits only std3, at Lean v4.34.1.
techniques.core_idea: Build determinants Delta_N of size 48N from moments of two kernels. Chebyshev rows with high Taylor contact cancel the zeta(2) term, so G in Q makes every entry rational. An arithmetic lower bound (prime valuations, PNT) is set against an analytic upper bound (logarithmic-potential energy, certified by exact rational data); nonvanishing comes from a Frobenius reduction mod p to three fixed matrices plus a finite certificate. The margin is razor thin: liminf L_N > -2.29084 against limsup L_N <= -2.290939875.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: None. The target must be a rational-linear combination of moments of explicit kernels, i.e. a period. x = 0.c(0)c(1)..._2 has no integral representation, and determinants built from its tails or digits have no analytic decay: its tails are pseudo-random 0/1 data.
techniques.obstacle: There is no analytic structure in c, and the method is blind to CA content. Verification caveat: I did not replay the comparator check (downloaded code is untrusted, and laptop limits apply). Litsey's extension is third-party evidence that the development builds. No peer review yet.
techniques.artifacts: Apache-2.0 Lean in openai/math, with the comparator challenge; Litsey's bound in Lean (Apache-2.0).

techniques.name: Separated-weight interpolation determinants: the claim mu(pi) = 2, and its extension mu(log r) = 2
techniques.origin: OpenAI internal model, family 017 'The irrationality exponent of pi is 2' (it also claims convergence of the Flint-Hills series). Extension by J. Liu, K. Jiang and P. Zhang (Wuhan/Peking) to logarithms of positive rationals.
techniques.date: OpenAI manuscript dated 2026-09-24, released 2026-10-06. Liu-Jiang-Zhang arXiv v1 2026-10-07, v2 2026-10-08.
techniques.ai_involvement: OpenAI's version is entirely model-produced, including a 4.3 MB Lean development (869 files) and a released reasoning-trace summary. Liu-Jiang-Zhang disclose no AI use, but cite OpenAI's manuscript as the source of the method.
techniques.proved: Claimed: for every nu > 2, |pi - p/q| >= q^(-nu) for all sufficiently large q (an ineffective threshold), so mu(pi) = 2. The repo ships ComparatorChallenges/PiExponent.lean, with config std3, and solution OAI.NumberTheory.PiExponent.Main. Third-party summaries disagree on whether 017 is formalized (cellcog says 'Not yet'), but the files are present in the 2026-10-06 commit. Liu-Jiang-Zhang claim mu(log r) = 2 for every rational r != 1, with no Lean and no review.
techniques.core_idea: This is Laurent-style interpolation-determinant transcendence machinery. It uses the curve z -> (e^z, z, ..., z), with interpolation centres at the putative rational approximations. An algebro-geometric interpolation theorem (blow-ups, Serre vanishing) guarantees a nonzero determinant. Its arithmetic lower bound contradicts its analytic upper bound.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: None. The method rests on the exponential map (e^(i pi) = -1, exp of rationals); the digits of x carry no such structure. Irrationality exponents are not even defined for x unless Problem 1 holds.
techniques.obstacle: There is no analytic structure in c. The claim is extraordinary and unrefereed, and no independent replay of the Lean has been reported.
techniques.artifacts: Apache-2.0 Lean and reasoning trace in openai/math.

surveys.notes:
I found nothing from 2024–2026, AI-assisted or not, that gives a route to Problem 1 through irrationality or transcendence. Searches covered erdosproblems.com (irrationality tag, accessed 2026-10-14/15), arXiv and GitHub. Downloads were read only; I did not build or execute any downloaded Lean, C or Python.

**Why nothing transfers.** In base 2 with digits {0,1}, "irrational iff not eventually periodic" is elementary (BinaryIrrational.lean), so all the difficulty is combinatorial and dynamical. Every method I surveyed needs one of four things:
- **Analytic structure.** The number must be a period, a moment, or a value of a D-finite or G-function (Calegari–Dimitrov–Tang, OpenAI's Catalan and π determinants, Apéry/conservative matrix fields, parameter displacement). For the center column, f(z) = Σ c(t) z^t is D-finite iff Problem 1 fails (Stephan's engine, the first entry), so no holonomic route can use f itself.
- **Arithmetic structure in the digits.** This means divisor or multiplicative functions with CRT or dilation identities (Erdős 1948, Tao–Teräväinen, #258). Rule 30 has no dilation identity, and rule 90 has one and is periodic.
- **Faster-than-geometric decay of terms** (Erdős–Straus, #1051). For rule 30 this leaves only the sufficient condition "c has arbitrarily long white (or black) runs". That is stronger than Problem 1 and of Problem 2 type. In the first 10⁷ bits the record runs are 22 white and 23 black, about log₂ n (computed with `/Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30tech/irrat-transc/scripts/runs.py`, checked against direct simulation).
- **Automatic or stammering digit structure** (Mahler/Adamczewski–Faverjon, Adamczewski–Bugeaud with the Subspace Theorem). These yield only "rational or transcendental", which is silent on the rational case, i.e. on Problem 1.

**What can be salvaged now.** All of it is CC0 Lean by Ralf Stephan with Claude Code, on toolchains v4.33.0-rc1 or later; port it by re-typing and reviewing, not by building the downloads.
1. Problem 1 ⟺ c is not P-recursive ⟺ Σ c(t) zᵗ is not algebraic over ℚ(z) ⟺ it is not rational over ℚ.
   - Source: rwst/Ceiling-Orbits, `RB/EventuallyPeriodic.lean` and `CITED/StanleyProof.lean`.
   - The pinned Mathlib lacks `PowerSeries.coeff_iterate_derivative` but has the `DifferentialAlgebra` instance Stanley's step uses.
2. Problem 1 ⟺ the Hankel determinants of c are nonzero infinitely often, over ZMod 2 or ℤ (`isRationalSeries_iff_kroneckerDet_eventually_zero`).
3. Problem 1 ⟺ Σ c(t) 2ᵗ ∈ ℤ₂ is irrational (`B3/DigitPeriodicity.lean`).
   - Do not import `BL/ConjugacyMap.lean` or `AB/StammeringSequences.lean`: both declare axioms. Check `#print axioms` after porting.
4. A finite Morse–Hedlund lemma: complexity ≤ n on a window of length ≥ 3n forces a long periodic factor. Useful for window certificates.
5. Cobham's linear-complexity bound, proved. It gives the strengthening chain: superlinear complexity ⇒ c not automatic ⇒ (Christol) Σ c(t) xᵗ transcendental over F₂(x).

**Conceptual lessons.**
- **Rational-base aperiodicity is the width-2 theorem in disguise.** Stephan's proof for the 3/2 word (window–residue rigidity plus a growth ceiling) is the same mechanism as the Jen–Kopra theorem that two adjacent rule 30 columns cannot both be eventually periodic. Left-permutivity plays the rigidity, the light-cone edge plays the ceiling. Width 1 needs one extra relation tying a neighbouring column to c. Condrey's defect identity gives it only where c(t) = 1, and rules 90/150/210 show any such relation must use the OR term.
- **Block certificates need zero entropy.** Stephan's confinement certificates show a lasso in a finite abstraction is harmless when an independent aperiodicity lemma kills its realisations. Rule 30 has such lemmas (`Rule30DrivenLeft.no_periodic_column`, Kopra width-2, Condrey). But this works only when the constrained abstraction has zero entropy, which the Q01/Absorption barriers exclude in general.
- **A natural stronger target:** a "Chowla conjecture" for c, meaning two-point decorrelation at every shift. It implies Problem 1 and sits below Problem 2.

**How far the AI claims hold up.**
- **Aletheia's Erdős sweep** (arXiv 2601.22401, 2026-02-05): of 200 graded answers, 63 were technically correct and 13 (6.5%) meaningfully correct. 8 of those 13 were literature finds or rediscoveries.
- **#333:** an earlier "AI solution" was already in a 1977 Erdős paper (Quanta, 2026-08-03).
- **Real AI-era irrationality results** are #1051 (golden-ratio threshold; Lean via Seed-Prover 1.5 and LeanMarathon), #258 (GPT-5.4 noticed that a Tao–Teräväinen theorem settles it), and counterexamples #251 and #263. Tao calls such Erdős solutions "the lowest hanging fruit".
- **OpenAI's 2026-10-06 release** (github.com/openai/math, Apache-2.0) claims Catalan's constant irrational and μ(π) = 2.
  - Both ship Lean developments with comparator configs that allow only the three standard axioms, at Lean 4.34.1. I did not replay either.
  - Three other manuscripts were withdrawn on 2026-10-07 for a sign error.
  - Secondary sources disagree on whether the π result (family 017) is formalized.
  - arXiv 2610.10192 (2026-10-07) extends the π argument to μ(log r) = 2: unrefereed and without Lean.
  - The same release's family 197 claims an injective non-surjective cellular automaton on a nonsofic group (Gottschalk). That is irrelevant to ℤ but may interest the CA-dynamics agents.
- **Z.-W. Sun's human Catalan proof** (arXiv 2609.04176) has a gap in its asymptotic bookkeeping (Wachs, arXiv 2609.22339, 2026-09-16).
- **Literature errors caught by AI formalization:** Stephan's Claude-assisted Lean found Theorem 1.3(i) of the unrefereed preprint Nair–Kumar–Rout (arXiv 2506.02898) false as printed.

**Lean kernel caveat for your project.** On 2026-07-25 an AI-assisted "Collatz disproof" got Lean to accept False via a kernel bug with nested inductive types; it was fixed in Lean 4.32.2 on 2026-07-28 (GIGAZINE, 2026-08-03). The Rule 30 projects pin Lean v4.30.0, before the fix. Ordinary elaboration was not exploitable, but agent-produced Lean should be re-checked with comparator or lean4checker on 4.32.2 or later.

**Not found:**
- Any 2024–2026 work on irrationality or transcendence of numbers whose digits come from a nonlinear cellular automaton.
- Any irrationality or transcendence problem among AlphaEvolve's 67 (searched the arXiv 2511.02864v3 PDF).
- Any Lean formalization of Christol's theorem or of Szegő/Pólya–Carlson.
- A full formalization of Mahler's method: it is formalized only modulo two lemmas.

I did not confirm the Annals volume of Adamczewski–Faverjon. erdosproblems.com pages can lag their forum threads (#263).

Everything I downloaded is in `/Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30tech/irrat-transc/` (the `dl-*` folders).

techniques.name: Number-wall (Hankel determinant) substitution certificate with a local-to-global check
techniques.origin: Claudemir de Souza Cavalcante (Universidade Federal do Para), answering J. Shallit's 2014 Open Problem 8 (GBP 100). It builds on F. Lunnon's number walls and his Dakota sequence (OEIS A301850, 2018), on Adiceam-Nesharim-Lunnon (Duke Math. J. 170, 2021) and on Garrett-Robertson (arXiv 2405.14454). AI: ChatGPT/Codex.
techniques.ai_involvement: Section 9 of the preprint: 'ChatGPT/Codex was used substantially in locating sources, reconstructing the certificate, implementing the verifier, checking the argument, and preparing this manuscript.' Shallit's talks page (note dated 2026-07-31) says the problem was solved 'using an LLM'.
techniques.proved: Over F_9 = F_3[u]/(u^2+1), let y_n = 1 + u d_n, where d_n is the bilateral Dakota sequence (a coding of a 2-uniform morphism on 4 letters). Every entry in rows m >= 0 of the number wall of y_n is nonzero, so every shifted Hankel determinant det(y_{k+i+j}) is nonzero. A rank-one degree bound then gives a 3-valued real sequence t + d_n with all shifted Hankel determinants nonzero: v1 proves this for transcendental t, v2 for all irrational t. This answers Shallit's problem affirmatively. Lunnon had already asserted the zero-free wall in OEIS A301850, and the paper claims only the reconstructed certificate, the verifier and the lift to the reals. The archive's certificate and verifier SHA-256 match the paper and MANIFEST. We did not run the verifier.
forms: no eventual linear recurrence over F_2 / unbounded linear complexity
non-rationality of sum c(t)x^t over F_2 (Kronecker-Hankel criterion)
techniques.core_idea: The number wall W_{m,n} (contiguous Toeplitz/Hankel determinants) obeys the local Desnanot-Jacobi recurrence W_{m,n}W_{m-2,n} = W_{m-1,n}^2 - W_{m-1,n-1}W_{m-1,n+1}. For an automatic input the wall is a 2-D substitution tiling. Guess the substitution from a finite wall segment: 1358 states coded by 8x8 blocks over F_9. Then verify finitely much: close the set of reachable 2x2 tile patterns (6202), check the identity on each (1,215,592 checks), check the boundary rows, and check that no state reachable in the upper half-plane codes a zero. Uniqueness of the recurrence lifts these finite checks to the infinite wall.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Problem 1 has exact Hankel forms. By Kronecker's criterion, which holds over any field, sum c(t)x^t is rational over F_2 iff det(c(i+j))_{0<=i,j<n} = 0 mod 2 for all large n. By Lunnon's window theory, c eventually satisfies an F_2-recurrence of order r iff row r of its F_2 number wall is eventually zero. So Problem 1 is equivalent to the F_2 wall of c having no infinite zero window, and a wall certificate of this kind would prove it. Our check on the first 16384 center bits (scripts/lcp_center.py): L_N = 8192 and max |L_n - floor((n+1)/2)| = 6. There are 4095 partial quotients of the F_2 continued fraction (their degrees equal the jump heights of the linear-complexity profile), with degree counts 2053, 1032, 498, 256, 125, 58, 34, 17, 13, 7, 1, 1 for degrees 1 to 12. That is the 2^-k law of a random sequence. The Wang-Massey perfect-profile condition fails at i = 2. All of this agrees with round 1 (|L_n - n/2| <= 9.5 up to 10^6, which forces T+P >= 499,998).
techniques.obstacle: A finite substitution certificate exists only if the wall is automatic, which forces c to be automatic. Then Walnut could decide Problem 1 outright. All evidence says c is not automatic: round 1 found all 2-kernel words distinct up to K = 13, and Nersissian (2026, our lit-recent notes) shows any LSD-first 2-DFAO needs >= 8191 states for a prefix of 131072. Low-complexity descriptions of the right half are refuted. The certificate is finite-state, so the Q01 barriers (finite abstractions, edge DFAs) apply to any use on the period-2 reduction. A finite piece of the wall gives only T+P bounds, and these are weaker than the bounds already proved.
