techniques.name: Lean-compiler feedback loop on formal statements (AlphaProof Nexus basic agent and full agent D)
techniques.origin: Google DeepMind: Tsoukalas, Kovsharov, Shirobokov, Surina, Firsching, Bérczi, Wagner, Wieser, Huang, Hubert, Balog, Kohli, Chaudhuri and others. Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search, arXiv 2605.22763.
techniques.date: arXiv v1 2026-05-21, v2 2026-06-08. Science publication on 2026-10-08 is reported by secondary sources only.
techniques.ai_involvement: Gemini 3.1 Pro prover subagents run 'Ralph loops': each edits a Lean sketch, Lean errors steer the next turn, and lessons are written back as comments between episodes. Agent B adds AlphaProof (an RL prover) to prove or refute subgoals. Agent C adds Gemini 3.0 Flash raters, Elo scores and P-UCB parent selection. Humans chose the problems and checked statement faithfulness after each solve.
techniques.proved: Agent D resolved 9 of 353 Erdős statements from formal-conjectures: #12(i), #12(ii), #125, a #138 variant, #152, #741(i), #741(ii), #846 and a #26 variant. It also resolved 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures (38 Lean files are released), Zanello's log-concavity case (3,2), a Graffiti leaf-number conjecture, and the anchored GDA O(1/t) rate. In ablation the basic agent A alone replicated all 9 Erdős solves. The repo's erdos_problems_attempted.txt lists the irrationality and digit problems #68, #243, #247, #251, #257, #264(ii), #267, #269 (variant), #1049 and #406 as attempted; none is among the solved. Verification: Lean, with SafeVerify statement checks.
forms: irrationality of the base-B real (closest attempted analogs failed)
techniques.core_idea: The input is a Lean file containing the target with sorry; the agent may edit only inside EVOLVE-BLOCK markers. The LLM refines the sketch, and compile errors serve as dense feedback. A validator rejects changed statements. EVOLVE-VALUE markers let the agent search a numeric parameter and its proof together; this is how it found a new step-size schedule.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Point this loop, or an open equivalent (OpenGauss/lean4-skills, Archon, LeanMarathon, Epoch's LeanOpenProblems harness), at our existing Lean propositions. Targets: CQ01 (Rule30PeriodTwoCoupled), Q01 beyond width 56 through chunked certificates, C3s001 (Rule30EtherThreeSkeleton), Q001/C3w(011) (Rule30EtherThreeLeft), AbsorptionT t001, and Absorption(0111) (Rule30Ether). Also use it to formalize third-party partial results into the catalog: Kopra 2023 (no two adjacent columns both eventually periodic for number-like configurations) and Condrey 2026 (fibre theorem). EVOLVE-VALUE-style joint search fits trap width, window size and transient bounds.
techniques.obstacle: Its successes are short elementary arguments for low-attention problems. It failed on every irrationality problem it attempted, and FrontierMath Erdős (Sep 2026) finds the best model resolves 2 of 68 curated open Erdős problems at $300. Barrier check: B1/B6 (finite abstractions and edge DFAs) and B2/JointBarrier (bounded windows) exclude the proof shapes these agents usually find. A successful sketch must carry global information from both halves, rule 30's OR, and the finite far-left support. That is exactly where the documented failure modes bite: the core difficulty gets offloaded into a sorry'd helper lemma that restates the target, and 'literature lemmas' turn out to be hallucinated.
techniques.artifacts: google-deepmind/alphaproof-nexus-results (Apache-2.0): 9 Erdős, 38 OEIS, Stacks Project and algebraic-geometry Lean files, plus natural-language PDFs and erdos_problems_attempted.txt. The framework itself is not released. google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Apache-2.0) states Problem 1 and Problem 2 for rule 30.

techniques.name: Closed-form space-time invariant proved by induction, for a single-seed ECA center column (OEIS A267581, rule 167)
techniques.origin: AlphaProof Nexus OEIS run (Google DeepMind). Re-proved independently in Epoch AI's OEIS Open (Tom Adamczewski) by Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash.
techniques.date: Lean file 2026-05. OEIS comment by Ralf Stephan 2026-05-28. OEIS Open arXiv 2608.11941, 2026-08-12.
techniques.ai_involvement: Fully autonomous: the APN agent, and the Epoch base agent on a $50 budget with each of three frontier models.
techniques.proved: The 2016 OEIS conjecture for the rule 167 center column from a single black cell: a(n) = 2a(n-1) + 1 - [n divides 2^(n+1)], previously tested only to n = 10^4. The proof is kernel-checked through SafeVerify.
forms: Problem 1 analog for another ECA (structured rule)
techniques.core_idea: Guess an explicit formula for the whole space-time: cell(t,x) = 1 - C(t-1,(x+t-2)/2) mod 2 on one parity class and 1 on the other. Prove ca_state t x = expected_state t x by induction on t using Pascal's rule mod 2. Evaluate at x = 0 with Lucas/Kummer: the relevant binomial is odd iff n is a power of 2.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This is the template for any rule whose single-seed space-time has a closed form. For rule 30 the nearest analog is Nersissian's Newton-support formula: c(n) = parity of #{r in S_(n+1) : r ⊆ n bitwise}, with S_m defined by an OR-convolution recursion (2026). An agent could formalize that identity and its bounds (min S_m = floor(m/2), max S_m ≤ F_(m+1) - 1) as catalog lemmas.
techniques.obstacle: Realization barrier T340: rules 90, 150 and 210 share every structural fact used and still have eventually periodic centers. Rule 167 is affine (a complemented Pascal-mod-2 pattern), so a closed-form or Lucas argument that never uses the OR term cannot reach rule 30. Rule 30's Newton support is as complex as the automaton (|S_44| = 64939) and does not decide periodicity.
techniques.artifacts: APN Lean file (Apache-2.0). Gold proof tests/data/gold_proofs/oeis_267581_conjecture_0.lean in epoch-research/LeanOpenProblems (MIT).

techniques.name: Finite-invariant, ratio-interval and coupling certificates for sequence conjectures (OEIS Open and AlphaProof Nexus)
techniques.origin: Epoch AI OEIS Open (Adamczewski) on the Tsoukalas et al. formalization of 492 OEIS conjectures; AlphaProof Nexus.
techniques.ai_involvement: Autonomous LMs in a minimal tool harness ($50 per attempt): Claude Opus 4.8 resolved 30%, GPT-5.5 26%, Gemini 3.5 Flash 22%. On the 100-problem Lite set at $200, the best (Claude Fable 5) scored 44%. Literature access and fancier agent loops did not help.
techniques.proved:
Resolved examples, all checked by SafeVerify in Lean:
- A271591 (runs of the second MSB of tribonacci numbers have lengths 4–5 and 3–4): ratio invariant 1.838 ≤ T(n+1)/T(n) ≤ 1.841 for n ≥ 9 plus base cases.
- A382590 (k-th prime factor eventually periodic): finite residue-state set mod 15 plus a growing 2-adic valuation.
- A100478 (the pentanacci-pi recurrence is ultimately periodic for every seed).
- A300997 (stabilization times of a mass-halving CA increase by 1 or 2): a coupled single extra unit of mass.

No model resolved A214560 (number of 0s in binary n^2 tends to infinity) or the A339602 XOR-reversal recurrence claim.
techniques.core_idea: Find a decidable finite object and prove by induction that it is invariant, then finish with finite computation. Examples are a finite residue set, an interval of ratios closed under the recurrence, or a single defect particle under a conservation law.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This class only works for low-complexity outputs, such as rotation codings or small-automaton outputs. Our C4 measurement gives p(64) = 702 for the right-half column 1 beside an alternating center, where a Sturmian word would have 65. The coupling trick behind A300997 needs mass conservation.
techniques.obstacle: B1 and B6 (every finite abstraction of ZBL states has a reachable lasso; no edge-DFA ranking) exclude this class for Q01. The additive barrier (no conservation law of range ≤ 10 for rule 30, ≤ 8 for rule 30^2) removes the coupling mechanism. The conjectures that every model failed on, such as zeros of n^2 in base 2, are the digit-randomness type that Problem 1 belongs to.
techniques.artifacts: epoch-research/LeanOpenProblems (MIT): 492 OEIS, Erdős and fc100open Lean statements, with a sandboxed Comparator/SafeVerify harness. epoch-research/LeanOpenProblems-results: all submissions and scores (no license file). APN OEIS Lean files (Apache-2.0).

techniques.name: Evolutionary program search for constructions (AlphaEvolve search and generalizer modes, FunSearch lineage)
techniques.origin: Google DeepMind AlphaEvolve. Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao, Wagner, Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale (arXiv 2511.02864). A related exploratory-programming case: Knuth's 'Claude's Cycles' (Claude Opus 4.6).
techniques.date: AlphaEvolve blog 2025-05-14 (arXiv 2506.13131). Tao et al. 2025-11-03, v3 2025-12-22. Knuth note dated 2026-02-28.
techniques.ai_involvement: Gemini models mutate programs scored by user-written evaluators. For the finite-field Kakeya construction, Deep Think proved the discovered construction correct and AlphaProof formalized it in Lean. In Knuth's case Claude Opus 4.6 ran brute force and simulated annealing, found a general construction for odd m, and Knuth proved it.
techniques.proved: Across 67 problems AlphaEvolve matched most best-known constructions and improved several (finite-field Kakeya/Nikodym, autocorrelation constants; 593 kissing spheres in 11D in the May 2025 report; slight improvements on Erdős #36, #507, #1097). The paper documents failures. The clearest is Erdős discrepancy: ±1 sequences of discrepancy 2 reached length 200 unguided and 380 with a multiplicativity hint, against the known optimum 1160 found by SAT.
forms: sub-questions: Q01 survival, traps for Absorption/AbsorptionT, walls for the period-3 ether, C3w(011)
factor complexity / shift orbit (search for long-lived constrained orbits)
techniques.core_idea: Evolve programs, not objects. In search mode each program is a time-boxed search heuristic, scored by the best object it finds. In generalizer mode a program must work for all n and is shown only small-n optima. The evaluator must be leak-proof, because the system exploits scoring loopholes (the paper's 'cheating phenomenon').
techniques.transfer_to_rule30:
Use it only where a graded score exists:
(a) Maximize survival time of ZBL starts beyond W = 71, to stress-test the empirical law 'dies by 2W+8' and Q01.
(b) Search right halves driven by 011 that make column 1 periodic, a counterexample hunt for C3w(011).
(c) Evolve SAT/BDD encodings or heuristics for traps of width 21–46 (t001, period-4 ether) and for period-3 walls wider than 28.
(d) Evolve whole-row potentials (lexicographic, position-weighted, multi-step), scored by the fraction of surviving double steps on which they decrease; send the survivors to a Lean agent.
techniques.obstacle: The 15 simple global monovariants already fail (our C7). B1, B2, B6 and JointBarrier rule out finite-state and bounded-window candidates, so only unbounded whole-row programs are admissible, and each must then be proved for every width. The discrepancy result shows SAT beats LLM evolution on binary-sequence constraint search, so put SAT inside the evolved heuristic. Evaluators approximating 'survives forever' by finite horizons are leaky and will be gamed.
techniques.artifacts: google-deepmind/alphaevolve_repository_of_problems and alphaevolve_results (Apache-2.0). Open re-implementations OpenEvolve and ShinkaEvolve (Apache-2.0).

techniques.name: Rapid-convergence irrationality by clearing denominators (Aletheia on Erdős #1051, human generalization, Seed-Prover 1.5 formalization)
techniques.origin: Google DeepMind Aletheia (Gemini Deep Think agent; Feng, Trinh, Luong et al.). Generalized by Barreto, Kang, Kim, Kovač and Zhang. Formalized by ByteDance Seed-Prover 1.5 and by Barreto.
techniques.ai_involvement: Aletheia found the #1051 proof autonomously. Deep Think and Aletheia proved a further generalization. Humans proved the golden-ratio threshold and the matching counterexamples. Seed-Prover 1.5 produced a 2990-line Lean proof, and Barreto formalized the original variant. Of the five graders of Aletheia's original output, one judged the step 'standard comparison theorems for linear recurrences' too unrigorous.
techniques.proved: If a_n is strictly increasing with liminf a_n^(1/2^n) > 1, then the sum of 1/(a_n a_(n+1)) is irrational. Humans sharpened this to limsup a_n^(1/φ^n) = ∞ and showed it is optimal. Aletheia's full sweep: 700 prompts, 212 flagged, 200 graded. Of those, 137 were flawed, 63 technically correct, 13 meaningful, and 4 novel (#652, #654, #1040, #1051). The authors say none of the four is paper-level.
techniques.core_idea: Suppose the sum is P/Q. The scaled tail x_m = (a_1...a_(m+1)) × tail_m is then a positive multiple of 1/Q. Double-exponential growth forces x_m → 0 along a subsequence, a contradiction. The threshold φ comes from balancing the product of the denominators against the size of the tail (Tao's heuristic on the forum).
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Apply it to S = Σ c(t) 2^-(t+1) = P/Q. Then Q·frac(2^m S) is an integer for every m, so any run of at least log2 Q equal symbols, followed by a change of symbol, contradicts rationality. Since the catalog proves that no column is eventually constant, Problem 1 follows from 'c has runs of unbounded length'. Our run of 60000 steps (frontier-ai-scripts/zero_runs.py) gives a zero-run record of 19 starting at t = 32198 and a one-run record of 21 at t = 37260, about log2 N; this is consistent but unproved.
techniques.obstacle: For 0/1 digits the Liouville margin is zero: denominators 2^m balance tails of size 2^-m × O(1) exactly. The method therefore only reduces Problem 1 to a stronger occurrence statement (unbounded runs), and Thue–Morse-like words show that non-periodicity does not imply unbounded runs. It conflicts with no barrier, but it gains no leverage either.
techniques.artifacts: ByteDance-Seed/Seed-Prover SeedProver-1.5/erdos_1051.lean (Apache-2.0). formal-conjectures ErdosProblems/1051.lean (Apache-2.0). Raw Aletheia outputs in google-deepmind/superhuman (Apache-2.0). YuanheZ/LeanMarathon (Apache-2.0) formalized theorems tied to #1051.

techniques.name: Irrationality and normality of dyadic series from local-pattern statistics (prime-pattern inputs)
techniques.origin: Tao and Teräväinen (human), Quantitative correlations and some problems on prime factors of consecutive integers (arXiv 2512.01739). Przemek Chojecki with GPT-5.4 Pro on Erdős #258. Johan Land on #251, with Gemini 3.8 Flash workers coordinated by Codex. StefanRinger (announced normality).
techniques.ai_involvement: GPT-5.4 Pro wrote the #258 note from prompts; Aristotle formalized it conditionally on the Tao–Teräväinen theorem. Land's Lean proof was written by about ten Gemini 3.8 Flash workers, coordinated and checked by Codex. Tao–Teräväinen is human work.
techniques.proved: Tao–Teräväinen: Σ ω(n)/2^n is irrational (Erdős #69, and #257 for the primes). #258: Σ τ(n)/(a_1...a_n) is irrational whenever a_n → ∞; the input is that τ(n+k) ≤ 2^(Ck) for infinitely many n and every k. #251 (Σ p_n/2^n irrational): proved assuming Kuperberg's uniform Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, Lean-checked as a conditional (Lean 4.34.0-rc2). Announced but unverified: normality of Σ P(g_n)/b^n under a prime-pattern hypothesis, and unconditional normality of a rough-number series.
techniques.core_idea: Rationality forces the tails T_N = Σ_(j≥1) f(N+j) 2^-j onto a lattice (1/Q)Z, with T_(N+1) = 2T_N − f(N+1). One then exhibits, infinitely often, local patterns that put a tail strictly between lattice points: long stretches of small values, or weighted gap tails approaching 6 from above. The patterns come from sieve and correlation theorems, or from a uniform prime-tuples hypothesis. Tao summarizes the #258 instance: infinitely often the tail decays faster than the reciprocal of the lcm of the earlier denominators.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: The same lattice argument applies to c: S is rational iff frac(2^m S) takes finitely many values. The prime-pattern input would be replaced by a theorem that specific local words of c recur infinitely often (unbounded runs, or more than P distinct words of some length). That is exactly the Morse–Hedlund / factor-complexity form already in our library.
techniques.obstacle: These proofs need a statistical theory of the sequence (sieves, Hardy–Littlewood, multiplicative correlations). For rule 30 no theorem gives the frequency of, or even guarantees infinitely many occurrences of, any long word in c, so the needed input is Problem-2-type. Note that formal-conjectures' Problem 2 (density 1/2) does not imply Problem 1 (0101... has density 1/2), whereas full normality does. For unbounded coefficients, the forum's 'Astra' countermodel shows that even short-block statistics do not force irrationality.
techniques.artifacts: beetree/math_erdos_251 (conditional Lean; no license file, so all rights reserved by default). Chojecki's GPT-5.4 Pro transcripts on Hugging Face (per the #258 forum). Aristotle's conditional gist for #258.

techniques.name: Free-parameter telescoping and sparse-perturbation countermodels (barrier constructions)
techniques.origin: Kovač and Tao, On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series (arXiv 2406.17593; Acta Math. Hungarica 175, 2025). Aristotle's Lean re-proof of the #264 partial result. GPT-5.4 Pro via Vjekoslav Kovač on a #251 variant. An 'Astra' write-up posted by forum user williamwkcook.
techniques.ai_involvement: Aristotle produced the formal re-proof. GPT-5.4 Pro found and wrote the telescoping counterexample with minimal orchestration. A model the poster calls Astra wrote the perturbation construction; the poster says it is not Lean- or Comparator-verified and has had no independent review.
techniques.proved: Kovač–Tao: 2^n is not an irrationality sequence; irrationality sequences exist for any growth F with F(n+1)/F(n) → ∞; and some sequence makes Σ 1/(a_n + t) rational for every rational t. GPT-5.4 Pro: g_n = o(p_n) does not force Σ p_n/(g_1...g_n) to be irrational. Astra (claimed): perturbing prime gaps on a set of upper Banach density zero lets Σ g_n/2^(n+1) hit any value in an interval while keeping congruences and short-block statistics.
techniques.core_idea: Keep one free parameter per scale (a correction e_n, or a recursively chosen c_n) and fix the parameters inductively so the series telescopes or lands on a target value. Any hypothesis that survives such perturbations therefore cannot imply irrationality.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: A ready method for new barrier theorems. Before investing in a strategy for Problem 1 or CQ01, have an AI construct a perturbed configuration that satisfies every fact the strategy uses but has an eventually periodic center. Our Rule30Realization.seed_perturbation, R30ProgA.edge_region_barrier and the truncated-stripe and c7 witnesses already follow this pattern.
techniques.obstacle: It prunes strategies; it cannot prove Problem 1. Perturbations of c must stay rule-30 orbits of finite configurations, which is far more rigid than perturbing free coefficients, so witnesses are harder to build than in the Erdős setting.
techniques.artifacts: Kovač–Tao paper. Aristotle #264 Lean, linked from the Tao wiki. Forum write-ups (no license).

techniques.name: Multi-scale density thinning by Diophantine alignment of two digit systems (Erdős #125)
techniques.origin: AlphaProof Nexus (Google DeepMind), full agent D.
techniques.ai_involvement: Autonomous. On this problem the full agent (AlphaProof plus evolution) clearly beat the basic agent. Humans changed 'density' to 'lower density' after the agent proved the natural-density reading (a misformalization).
techniques.proved: A + B, where A has only digits 0,1 in base 3 and B only digits 0,1 in base 4, has lower density 0. The question had been open since 1996.
forms: irrationality / digit structure of the base-B real (analogy only)
techniques.core_idea: Split a at base-3 digit k and b at base-4 digit m, choosing 3^k ≈ 4^m by Dirichlet approximation of log 4/log 3. Every x < 3^k N_0 in A+B is then y·3^k + r with y in (A+B)∩[0,N_0) and r in a short range. So the counting density drops by a factor of at most 0.99 per scale; iterating drives it to 0.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Rule 30 has native 2-adic scales: rows at powers of two restart the right-edge pattern, and right diagonals have power-of-two periods. A renormalization argument would show that some density-like quantity of an eventually periodic c must shrink across the scales 2^k.
techniques.obstacle: The argument needs exact self-similarity: a digit-restricted set factors as top·base^k + bottom. c has no known self-similarity, and Nersissian notes his diagonal-period theorems do not reach the moving center. Rule 90's exact self-similarity together with its eventually periodic center (barrier T340) shows self-similarity alone cannot decide Problem 1.
techniques.artifacts: APN repo (Apache-2.0): erdos_125 Lean file and NaturalLanguageProofs/ErdosProblems/erdos125.pdf.

techniques.name: Kummer/Lucas carry counting with a counting choice of n (Erdős #728, #729, #730)
techniques.origin: Kevin Barreto operating GPT-5.2 Pro and Harmonic Aristotle; writeup by Nat Sothanaphan (arXiv 2601.07421). Liam Price with GPT-5.5 Pro for #730.
techniques.ai_involvement: GPT-5.2 Pro produced the argument and Aristotle the Lean proof; a human wrote it up. The #730 candidate has not been reviewed.
techniques.proved: #728: for 0 < C1 < C2 there are infinitely many a, b, n with εn ≤ a, b ≤ (1−ε)n, a!b! | n!(a+b−n)! and C1 log n < a+b−n < C2 log n. It is Lean-checked, and similar literature (Pomerance 2014) was found afterwards. #730 (claimed): ≫ x^(1/2) values n ≤ x for which C(2n,n) and C(2n+2,n+1) have the same prime divisors.
techniques.core_idea: Reduce to the binomial divisibility C(m+k,k) | C(2m,m) and treat one prime at a time. By Kummer, v_p(C(2m,m)) counts the carries when doubling m in base p. Count the m in [M,2M] that are 'carry-rich but spike-free' for every p ≤ 2k.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Rule 30's Newton-support form, c(n) = XOR over r in S_(n+1) with r ≤ n of C(n,r) mod 2, makes c a Lucas-type sum, so 2-kernel subsequences c(2^a j + r) are natural objects. Nersissian found 8191 distinct kernel words for a ≤ 12, so any 2-DFAO for c needs at least 8191 states. Carry counting could prove 'some n in each dyadic block has property X'.
techniques.obstacle: Existence by counting proves 'some n' statements, not the exclusion of every period. The Lucas structure is shared with rule 90 (barrier T340). S_m comes from an OR-convolution recursion that is as hard to control as the automaton itself.
techniques.artifacts: Aristotle Lean files for #728/#729, linked from the Tao wiki (formal-conjectures statements are Apache-2.0). arXiv 2601.07421.

techniques.name: Counterexample-first reasoning checked by exact certificates (AI disproofs of long-standing conjectures)

techniques.proved: #90: point sets with at least n^(1+c) unit distances, a Lean-verified disproof; Claude Mythos's later version reportedly covers only a weaker form and is contested. forms: sub-questions: Q01 survival law 2W+8, C3w(011), C3s001, AbsorptionT t001, period-3 'no wall', right-half block law
techniques.core_idea: Prompt neutrally ('prove or refute'). Let the model search for an explicit object with heavy computation. Accept it only with an exact certificate (Lean decide or compute, or a CAS check), never on the narrative.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Aim it at our sub-hypotheses, not at Problem 1 itself. Candidates: every ZBL start of width W dies by 2W+8; C3w(011); C3s001; AbsorptionT for t001; the period-3 ether has no wall; the right-half block law. Round 1 already lost claims to counterexamples (the C3 off-by-one, the single-trap claim, and p_c(20) = 2^20), so an early refutation saves a dead reduction.
techniques.obstacle: Problem 1 itself is strongly supported: T + P ≥ 16359 is kernel-checked, and P ≤ 4096 with T ≤ 8192 is excluded. techniques.name: Adversarial proof checking: Comparator challenges, kernel replay, axiom whitelists, test lemmas
techniques.origin: Lean FRO (Comparator, lean4export, lean4checker); nanoda independent kernel; Epoch AI harness; OpenAI ten-proofs; SafeVerify; LeanParanoia; AlphaProof Nexus 'test lemmas'. Thomas Hales guest post on Tao's blog.
techniques.date: Comparator repo created 2025-06-06. Lean 4.32.1 on 2026-07-22 and 4.32.2 on 2026-07-28 fixed kernel soundness bugs. Hales post 2026-10-09.
techniques.ai_involvement: This infrastructure exists to check AI-generated proofs. Patrick Hulin found kernel bug #14484 with GPT-5.6 Sol. An AI-assisted 'Collatz disproof' (xrchz/CollatzLean) exploited kernel bug #14576 together with a separate nanoda bug.
techniques.proved: No mathematics. It established the acceptance practice: a proof counts only if it replays through a pristine kernel in a sandbox against a trusted statement file, with identical dependencies and axioms within {propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice}, and with the agent and the checker in separate containers. FrontierMath Erdős §3.3 lists the attack classes this defeats: tampering with the environment, compile-time code, proving a different statement, redefining dependencies, assuming the result, and bypassing the kernel (debug.skipKernelTC, addDecl metaprogramming, native_decide/implemented_by).
techniques.core_idea: Separate the trusted statement from the untrusted proof. Replay the proof in a sandbox, compare declarations, and whitelist axioms. Add test lemmas that pin definitions to known values, re-check with an independent kernel, and have a human audit statement fidelity.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30:
Our catalog and equivalents library run on Lean v4.30.0, which predates the July 2026 kernel fixes. Steps:
- Write Comparator challenge JSONs for Problem1 and for each equivalence (base-B irrational, F_2 power series, Morse–Hedlund, rules 86/135/149, complement).
- Re-check everything under Lean 4.32.2 or later with a current nanoda.
- Add test lemmas: first binary digits of the real, first coefficients of the series, and the A051023 prefix, as formal-conjectures' centerColumn_prefix does.
- Extend our source scan (sorry, native_decide, axiom, extern, unsafe, implemented_by) to run_cmd, addDecl and debug.skipKernelTC.
techniques.obstacle: None mathematical. Trust still rests on the kernel and the checker, and summer 2026 showed both can have bugs. Statement fidelity still needs a human audit.

techniques.name: Prompting and process patterns: neutral prove-or-refute, context de-identification, scaffolding, cross-domain reframing
techniques.origin: Woodruff, Cohen-Addad, Mirrokni et al. (Google), Accelerating Scientific Research with Gemini: Case Studies and Common Techniques (arXiv 2602.03837).
techniques.ai_involvement: Gemini Deep Think working with researchers.
techniques.proved: Case studies in theoretical CS, optimization, economics and physics, mainly settling or refuting conjectures; for example 'Simplex is best' for Euclidean Steiner trees via Kirszbraun, and a refuted conjecture in online submodular welfare. Documented failure modes: confirmation bias; confident technical hallucinations; alignment friction (refusing problems it recognizes as famous open ones); hallucinated references.
techniques.core_idea: Decompose the problem into verifiable lemmas and give a scaffold. Prompt neutrally, and remove identifying context so the model actually tries the problem. Ask for analogies from other fields, and verify numerically or formally in a loop.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Pose Q01, CQ01 and C3w(011) as anonymous statements about a boundary-driven nonlinear shift, not as 'Rule 30 Prize', to avoid refusals and literature-retrieval loops. Ask for cross-domain reframings: 2-adic and odometer dynamics, p/q automata, Mahler functions, and the 'Φ(f) is never finitely supported' form of Q01.
techniques.obstacle: These are process gains only. The success stories are cases where a known theorem (Kirszbraun, Stone–Weierstrass) closes the gap, and no such tool is known for rule 30.

surveys.notes:
I found no frontier-AI technique, verified or announced up to 2026-10-15, that directly attacks Problem 1 or any of its equivalent forms.

**Coverage.** No result touches rule 30, nonlinear cellular automata, combinatorics on words, symbolic dynamics, F_2 linear complexity, the 2-adic form, Christol or Problem 3. The closest are below.
- **Irrationality via growth or prime patterns:** Erdős #1051, #258, and #251 (conditional).
- **Digit-set density:** Erdős #125.
- **Two cellular-automaton results, both in OEIS:**
  - A267581, the center column of rule 167. Rule 167 is affine, so a closed form exists.
  - A300997, a mass-halving CA, proved via a conservation law.
- **Rule 30 itself** has been in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Other/Rule30.lean) only since 2026-09-07. No AI attempt on it is reported.

**Calibration.**
- FrontierMath Erdős (arXiv 2609.25050): the best model (GPT-6 Astra) resolved 2 of 68 curated open problems at $300, and 5 of 68 after more than $220k.
- AlphaProof Nexus solved 9 of 353 Erdős statements. It failed on every irrationality and digit problem it attempted: #68, #243, #247, #251, #257, #264(ii), #267, #269, #1049, #406.
- Aletheia: 13 of 200 graded answers were meaningful (6.5%) and 4 were novel, none at paper level.
- OEIS Open: about 30% of low-attention OEIS conjectures resolved at $50 each. Every model failed the digit-randomness conjecture A214560 (zeros in binary n² tend to infinity). Problem 1 belongs to this failing class.

**What produced verified results:**
- Lean-in-the-loop agents checked by Comparator or SafeVerify. A basic loop matched elaborate agents.
- Explicit counterexamples with exact certificates (unit distance, Jacobian in dimension 3, #619, OEIS disproofs).
- Literature identification.
- Short elementary arguments for low-attention problems.
- Closed-form invariants proved by induction for structured sequences.
- Pipelines where a model produces a natural-language proof that is then formalized, for example GPT-5.x with Aristotle.

**Documented failure modes:**
- **Misformalized or trivialized statements:** 50 of Aletheia's 63 technically correct answers were vacuous; #124 was solved in a weaker form; the "density" reading had to be fixed for #125 and #741; #263 was misstated.
- **Sorry-offloading** into a helper lemma that restates the target (AlphaProof Nexus).
- **Hallucinated lemmas and citations:** First Proof batch 3 had adequate citations in only 4 of 10 Astra answers.
- **Rediscovery and "subconscious plagiarism":** #333, #397, #281, #1026, #897, #1089.
- **Overclaims:**
  - GPT-5 Erdős post, Oct 2025, deleted after Bloom called it "a dramatic misrepresentation": https://the-decoder.com/leading-openai-researcher-announced-a-gpt-5-math-breakthrough-that-never-happened/
  - Bubeck's GPT-5 Pro 1.5/L step-size bound, Aug 2025, when the authors' v2 had already proved 1.75/L: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16072
  - First Proof batch 1: organizers confirmed 2 of 10, OpenAI claimed 6.
  - CDC proof unverified; Navier–Stokes contested.
- **Verifier and kernel exploits:**
  - AlphaEvolve's "cheating phenomenon".
  - Lean bug #14484, found with GPT-5.6 Sol and fixed in 4.32.1 on 2026-07-22.
  - False Collatz disproof via bug #14576 plus a separate nanoda bug, fixed in 4.32.2 on 2026-07-28.
- **Prompt effects:** confirmation bias, and refusal to attempt problems the model recognizes as famous.

**Barrier cross-check.**
- Finite-invariant, interval-ratio and coupling certificates are excluded by B1, B6, B2, JointBarrier and the additive-law barrier. This is the class behind most AI sequence proofs.
- Closed-form, Lucas/carry and self-similarity arguments are excluded by realization barrier T340 unless they use rule 30's OR.
- Analytic irrationality (tail and denominator methods, prime-pattern lattice arguments) has zero margin for 0/1 digits. It only reduces Problem 1 to stronger occurrence statements, such as unbounded runs.
- **My check:** 60000 steps give a zero-run record of 19 at t=32198 and a one-run record of 21 at t=37260, about log2 N. Script: /Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30tech/frontier-ai-scripts/zero_runs.py. Its prefix matches A051023.
- No AI technique escapes the barriers on its own. The levers that remain are search on sub-hypotheses with graded scores, formalization, and verification hygiene.

**Recommended actions, most valuable first:**
1. Re-check the catalog and the equivalents library under Lean 4.32.2 or later. Both are on v4.30.0, which predates the kernel fixes. Use Comparator plus a current nanoda, add a Comparator challenge JSON and test lemmas for each equivalence, and extend the source scan to run_cmd, addDecl and debug.skipKernelTC.
2. Run an open Lean agent (OpenGauss/lean4-skills, Archon, LeanMarathon, or Epoch's LeanOpenProblems harness) on formalization targets: Kopra 2023, the Condrey fibre theorem, Nersissian's Newton-support identity, Fatou/Pólya–Carlson and Christol. Then try it on CQ01, C3s001, AbsorptionT t001 and Absorption(0111).
3. Use AlphaEvolve-style search (OpenEvolve or ShinkaEvolve, with SAT inside the evolved heuristics):
   - long-surviving ZBL starts beyond W=71;
   - traps of width 21–46;
   - period-3 walls wider than 28;
   - right halves driven by 011 that would refute C3w(011);
   - whole-row potentials scored by the fraction of steps on which they decrease.
4. Use neutral, de-identified prompts, and an author–critic reviewer before formalizing any natural-language step.

**Not independently verified by me:**
- The Science publication of AlphaProof Nexus (secondary sources only).
- Claude Mythos on #90 (weaker version, contested).
- The Jacobian counterexample (computational checks, no peer review).
- Astra's #251 countermodel and Ringer's normality claim (forum posts).
- Math Inc's timing claims.
- The CDC and Navier–Stokes results.
- The #730 candidate.
- The Tao wiki counts, which are data as of 2026-06-30.

**Where things are:**
- Downloads are untrusted, kept under /Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30tech/frontier-ai/ in dl_* folders, and were never executed.
- The writeup text extract used for the barrier check is /Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30_writeup_text.txt.
- BB(5) and the Equational Theories Project (arXiv 2512.07087) are adjacent automated-proof patterns outside this area.

techniques.name: Masked Jen and its window, finitary, or-column, driven-left and white-seed forms
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize attempt (VibeProof/Rule30Prize), round 1 (agents new-ideas, jen-generalized, absorbing-left, complexity, algebraic), modules Rule30MaskedJen, Rule30DrivenLeft, Rule30WhiteSeed on top of Rule30Jen. People: Nikolay Murzin (direction) with Claude Code agents (Anthropic). Base theorem: E. Jen, 'Global properties of cellular automata', J. Stat. Phys. 43 (1986) 219-242.
techniques.ai_involvement: Claude Code multi-agent workflow (Anthropic Claude; the archive does not record model IDs). Attack agents found the masked and window forms and proved them in core Lean 4.30; separate adversarial verifier agents re-derived and attacked each claim. A verifier refuted one corollary in Lean (off-by-one gap threshold in the doubling-window corollary), which was repaired (C3Rescue.lean). The human set the goal and accepted only kernel-checked results with standard axioms.
techniques.proved: masked_jen: if column i has period P from T, column i+1 is not P-periodic from T on the white times of column i (Lean; axioms propext, Quot.sound, re-checked 2026-10-15). orCol_not_eventuallyPeriodic: column i eventually periodic implies col_i OR col_(i+1) is not. window_jen (no periodicity assumed): for t1 < t2 the windows (c on [t1,t1+t2], c OR col1 on [t1,t1+t2)) differ. finitary_jen: columns 0 and 1 are never both P-periodic on [n-P,2n]. periodic_window: a P-periodic c has a white-time column-1 defect in every [n,2n). Rule30DrivenLeft.no_periodic_column: a left half driven by any eventually periodic boundary from a finite nonzero start has no eventually periodic column (no left absorption). Rule30WhiteSeed.problem1_30_or_135: Problem 1 holds for rule 30 from a black seed or for rule 135 from a black seed.
forms: per-word form problem1_iff_no_word: every word exclusion in the archive ends with this lemma
F2 linear-recurrence form, as a two-sequence statement: (x^P-1)C(x) a polynomial forces (x^P-1)E(x) non-polynomial for E the series of c OR col1
rules 86/135/149: only a disjunction with rule 135 from a BLACK seed (column -1), which Symmetry.lean correctly flags as not known equivalent
techniques.core_idea: Rule 30 is left-permutive: cell(t,i-1) = cell(t+1,i) XOR (cell(t,i) OR cell(t,i+1)). So column i+1 enters the leftward reconstruction only through the OR, i.e. only at the white times of column i. If column i is periodic and column i+1 is periodic on those white times, periodicity propagates to every column on the left, and the left edge (one new black cell per step) forbids that.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: It is the endpoint any absorption-type exclusion of a word w must reach: show that column 1 becomes periodic at the white phases of w. It fixes exactly what an external technique has to deliver. Barrier check: Jen's argument holds verbatim for rules 90, 150 and 210, whose centers are eventually constant (Rule30Realization.barrier), so masked Jen can only be the last step; the content must come from an OR-specific theorem about the right half. The window form shows the left side holds nothing more: every pair (c, col1) extends uniquely to a left field, and only the time-0 finiteness condition remains (round-1 result C11).
techniques.obstacle: It needs a second periodic object. For every word of length 2-7 the right-strip relaxation has histories whose white-phase column-1 output is aperiodic (computed to width 16, 20 for 0001), and under period-2 driving the true right half's output has positive entropy (about 0.07 bits per white time). So masked Jen alone excludes no period of 2 or more.
techniques.artifacts: Lean (core 4.30, no Mathlib): VibeProof/Rule30Prize/lean/Ruliology/CellularAutomata/Rule30MaskedJen.lean (masked_jen, masked_jen_center, orCol_not_eventuallyPeriodic, effective_boundary, effective_step, window_jen, periodic_window, finitary_jen), Rule30Jen.lean, Rule30DrivenLeft.lean, Rule30WhiteSeed.lean; research/verify-c3-doubling/C3Rescue.lean (sharp window). License: github.com/sw1sh/vibe-proof is public with no license file (GitHub API: license null).

techniques.name: Effective boundary c(t) AND c(t+1) and the reduction of short words to left-only problems
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize round 1 (agent small-periods; verifier verify-C1-effbdry-rigor), extended in round 2 and the final batch. Modules Rule30MaskedJen, Rule30PeriodTwo, Rule30PeriodFourSkeleton, Rule30EtherThreeLeft, Rule30EtherThreeSkeleton, Rule30PeriodTwoCoupled. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Found and proved by Claude Code agents in round 1; adversarially verified; the derived reductions were written by round-2 and final-batch agents and re-verified by the synthesis and verifier agents.
techniques.proved: effective_boundary: cell(t,-1) OR c(t) = cell(t,-1) OR (c(t) AND c(t+1)) (uses no axioms); effective_step: column -1 evolves with c(t) AND c(t+1) in place of c(t). Hence c(t)=1 implies cell(t,-1) = NOT c(t+1), and for a period word with no cyclically adjacent 1s the left half from the onset is the autonomous zero-boundary left half (ZBL) started from a finite row. Reductions in Lean: Q01 implies no eventual period 2 (not_eventually_period_two_of_Q01); CQ01 (faithful coupled version) implies no period 2 and Q01 implies CQ01; C3(w) for 0001, 0011, 0111 implies no least period 4 (least_period_four_of_C3); Q001 or C3s001 excludes a 001 tail; C3w(011) excludes a 011 tail. All of these hypotheses are open.
forms: period-2 exclusion, equivalently c(t) = c(t+1) for infinitely many t
techniques.core_idea: Because OR saturates, column 0 matters to the left half only when column -1 is white, and there the update equals the one with boundary c(t) AND c(t+1). For words with isolated ones this effective boundary is identically white, so a periodic tail would force a finite, autonomous half-line system to keep column -1 black at prescribed times forever.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This is the plug where any technique of the form 'a finite orbit cannot satisfy a shift-invariant constraint forever' attaches to Problem 1, word by word. Barrier check: the left-only problems are blocked for finite-state, local-ranking, edge-DFA and additive invariants (Rule30ZeroBoundaryBarriers; additive barrier) and for edge structure plus short windows (edge_region_barrier). Q01 relaxes period 2 (it drops the right half), so it could be false while period 2 is impossible; the faithful statement is CQ01.
techniques.obstacle: Each reduced statement is about every orbit of a positive-entropy constrained system: the constrained ZBL set is conjugate to the full shift and survival statistics match an unbiased coin to 0.2%; exhaustive searches give death by 2W+8 for widths W <= 71 (Q01), and by about 2.5-4W for the period-3 problems (W <= 37/70).
techniques.artifacts: Lean: Rule30MaskedJen.lean, Rule30PeriodTwo.lean (Q01, golden, not_eventually_period_two_of_Q01), Rule30PeriodFourSkeleton.lean (C3, least_period_four_of_C3), Rule30EtherThreeLeft.lean, Rule30EtherThreeSkeleton.lean, Rule30PeriodTwoCoupled.lean. Death-time searches: research/progA-backdet/dfs.c, research/A-monovariant/dfs.c, research/A-invsearch/maxdeath.c, research/p3-ether/c/ldfs.c. No license file in the repo.

techniques.name: Strip certificates (rank and position labelling on the right-strip graph) and their soundness
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize round 1 (agents new-ideas, jen-generalized, small-periods; three verifier agents per claim); modules Rule30StripCertificates, Rule30StripCertificateTable; final-batch word_lemma in Rule30EtherTrap. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Designed, implemented in C/Python and proved sound in Lean by Claude Code agents; certificate searches cross-checked by independent programs written by different agents; three verifiers reproduced the negative (no-certificate) counts.
techniques.proved: Cert.sound: for a word w of length P and width b, take the graph on (phase, columns 1..b) with column b+1 a free input. A rank that never increases along edges plus a position labelling that advances exactly at white phases on rank-preserving edges, determines column 1 there and satisfies G^(mP) = id excludes w for every transient and phase. problem1_iff_no_word: Problem 1 holds iff no nonempty word is an eventual period word. Kernel-checked exclusions of 33 words of length 8-13 (e.g. 00000011, 01111111, 0^10 1, 000000000101 and the 30-word certTable). About 180 more words (0^k 1 for 10 <= k <= 30, 0 1^k, ...) are certified by two independent programs but are not in Lean. Limit (computer, three reproductions): no certificate exists for any primitive word of length 2-7 at widths <= 16 (<= 20 for 0001), nor of length 9 at widths <= 16, because each strip graph has an SCC with two cycles whose white-phase outputs do not commute; Lean's word_lemma turns such cycles into an aperiodic path inside any closed set.
forms: F2 form: excludes specific eventual linear recurrences x^T(x^P-1) with a given periodic numerator
techniques.core_idea: Replace the unknown far right half by an adversary who chooses column b+1 freely. If along every infinite path of this finite graph column 1 at the white phases is forced to become periodic, masked Jen excludes the word. Soundness holds because the true history is one of the paths.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Useful for a census of easy words and, with a pumping lemma, for uniform infinite families; it cannot reach periods 2-7. Barrier check: this is exactly the local/strip class that the local-obstruction computation and word_lemma show cannot work for short words, and it discards the finiteness of the right half that the realization theorem says any proof needs.
techniques.obstacle: Short words are uncertifiable at every computed width; only 2-3% of words of length 12-16 are certifiable, and every certified word contains a run of at least 6 equal symbols.
techniques.artifacts: Lean: Rule30StripCertificates.lean (Cert, Cert.sound, not_eventually_word_strip, problem1_iff_no_word, not_eventually_00000011, not_eventually_000000000101), Rule30StripCertificateTable.lean, Rule30EtherTrap.lean (word_lemma, escapes_of_certOK). Code: research/newideas (strip_scan.c, cert.py), research/generalize-jen (scc_scan.py, strip_scan.py, certgen.py), research/smallperiods (reach3.c, reach_py2.py), research/verify-C4-counterexample/lean/C4a-C4c.lean. No license file.

techniques.name: Traps for the driven right half and the Absorption statements (least period 4 and the word 001)
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize round 1 (new-ideas, small-periods), round 2 (p4-edge, p4-nested-scc) and final batch (p3-ether, kernel-certify-r2), each with adversarial verifiers. Modules Rule30Ether, Rule30EtherTrap, Rule30EtherTrapWidth20, Rule30EtherThreeTrap, Rule30EtherThreeReach. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Traps found by Claude Code agents with C searches; closure and soundness proved in Lean; the round-1 claim 'every finite right half enters the trap' was refuted independently by two round-2 agents (Lean and a relay counterexample); final-batch verifiers rebuilt all modules and re-ran the entry statistics with their own code.
techniques.proved: Closed, consistently labelled trap sets for 0001, 0011, 0111 (109, 188, 188 states at widths 16, 16, 14) and for 001 the trap t001 (815 states on a 47-cell strip, period 21): closed under every far input, with column 1 at white phases a fixed function of a time label; if c is eventually w-periodic the true strip never enters them (research/verify-p4traps-rigor/P4Traps.lean; Rule30EtherThreeTrap.trap_001). The empty right half reaches t001 at time 1270 (t001_reached). never_enters_S0001/S0011/S0111: explicit finite right halves never enter the round-1 traps. With 24 kernel-checked certificates the pure ether lies in no trap of width <= 20 (pure_ether_not_in_trap_*). Absorption(w) and AbsorptionT(t001) are Lean Props; least_period_four_of_absorption and not_eventually_001_of_absorption show what they would exclude. Both are open.
forms: per-word form: least period 4 (0001, 0011, 0111) and the word 001
techniques.core_idea: A trap is a set of right-strip states that the strip can never leave, whatever enters from the far right, and on which column 1 at white phases is periodic. Entering it after the onset would supply the second periodic object masked Jen needs. All that is open is entry.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This is the only frontier where the true right half empirically always absorbs: every finite right half with support in [1,12] enters the ether+wall family (support in [1,16]: certified absorbed into closed labelled sets), and every true right half at T <= 300,000, with maximum delays 1017, 1869, 829 for 0001, 0011, 0111; all 18,258 runs for 001 enter t001 (delays up to 201,756). The best single partial target is Absorption(0111): one alignment, no skeleton, shortest delays. Barrier check: trap-avoiding strip paths keep the full growth rate, the pure ether avoids every trap of width <= 20, and entry happens before any right-edge signal can arrive (T >= about 2000), so a proof must use the finite support of the right half in the chaotic bulk; no fixed-width strip ranking can work.
techniques.obstacle: Absorption is a nucleation theorem for a chaotic driven system: every finite orbit must eventually build a wall. Compactness only yields infinite avoiders such as the pure ether. For 0101 (about 3% absorb) and 011 (never) nothing is absorbed, so traps cannot settle periods 2 or 3.
techniques.artifacts: Lean: Rule30Ether.lean (Absorption, absorption_excludes, least_period_four_of_absorption, never_enters_*), Rule30EtherTrap.lean, Rule30EtherTrapWidth20.lean, Rule30Certificates/EtherTrap0-5.lean, Rule30EtherThreeTrap.lean, Rule30EtherThreeReach.lean; research/verify-p4traps-rigor/P4Traps.lean. Data/code: research/B-edge-trap (cert_{0001,0011,0111}_20.txt, verify_cert.py), research/progB-avoid (scc_an.c; bulk bad-SCC files regenerable), research/p3-ether/c (entry3.c, closure.c, trap_export.py, xcheck_entry.py, rwalk47.c). No license file.

techniques.name: Ethers and walls: the 7x4 and 12x3 periodic backgrounds and the W109 wall
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize round 2 (agent p4-edge; cross-checked by synthesis-2) and final batch (p3-ether). Modules Rule30Ether, Rule30EtherThree, Rule30EtherThreeNoWall, Rule30PeriodTwoCoupled. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Discovered by a Claude Code agent analysing why period-4 traps exist; proved in Lean; the synthesis agent found that the same ether is the period-2 infinite witness and the two-sided barrier witness; a verifier narrowed an overstated 'no wall exists' to widths <= 12 (Lean) and <= 28 (search).
techniques.proved: ether_rule: the 7x4 ether (columns 0011, 0110, 1101, 0101, 0011, 0001, 0001) is a rule-30 orbit, and 0001, 0011, 0111 and 0101 are among its columns up to a time shift. wallOK_true: the 109-state, 13-cell wall W109 is closed under every right input. ether_wall_trap / no_ether_wall_entry: if c = w^inf from T, the true right half never shows ether columns 1..k (k in a fixed class mod 7) followed by a W109 state, an infinite trap family that explains every observed trap width. ether3_rule and alignments_001/011_complete: the 12x3 ether carries 001 and 011 with exactly six alignments each; no_wall_le_12 (Lean) and no wall up to width 28 (two exhaustive searches). ether_coupled_witness: the ether is an infinite configuration meeting every period-2 constraint; its truncations are the witnesses of the two-sided barrier. Computer census (not Lean): small ethers carry 01, 0001, 0011, 0111 (7,4), 001, 011 (12,3), 01011 (5,5), 00001, 01111 (15,5), 15 words of period 7 and more.
forms: per-word form for periods 2, 3, 4 (conditional exclusions); further words of periods 5, 7, 8, 9 through the census
techniques.core_idea: Every short candidate period word occurs as a column of a spatially and temporally periodic rule-30 pattern (an ether). An ether segment next to the center plus a closed wall strip is a trap of unbounded width. Conversely the pure infinite ether satisfies every local constraint forever, which is why local methods fail.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This is the structure a hypothetical periodic tail would have to settle into, and the right vocabulary for a nucleation proof: Absorption(w) says every finite right half driven by w^inf eventually builds ether plus wall. Walls for the other ethers in the census would give conditional exclusions of more words. Barrier check: the ether is itself the counter-witness for local, strip and edge-window arguments (JointBarrier uses its truncations), so a proof must explain why a finite right half cannot keep a chaotic front against the boundary forever.
techniques.obstacle: The period-3 ether has no wall up to width 28, 011 never absorbs, and 0101 absorbs in about 3% of runs, so ether plus wall reaches only least period 4 (and 001 through the non-ether trap t001). The missing step is the same Absorption theorem.
techniques.artifacts: Lean: Rule30Ether.lean (ether_rule, wallOK, trap_invariant, ether_wall_trap, no_ether_wall_entry), Rule30EtherThree.lean, Rule30EtherThreeNoWall.lean, Rule30PeriodTwoCoupled.lean; original research/B-edge-trap/lean/EtherWall.lean. Code: research/B-edge-trap, research/synth-r2/ether_check.py and relay_family.py, research/p3-ether/c/wall3.c and wall3b.c. No license file.

techniques.name: Zero-boundary left half: realization bijection, conjugacy to the full shift, and Q01 = LR = BWR
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize round 2, three independent formalizations (agents q01-backward, q01-reconstruction, q01-monovariant) plus verifier supplements, deduplicated into module Rule30ZeroBoundary. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Three Claude Code agents formalized the same object in three encodings without coordination; verifiers and the synthesis agent re-compiled all of them; the integration agent merged them into one module with glue theorems.
techniques.proved: Realization: the column next to the wall determines the whole ZBL history, and every column sequence occurs exactly once (recon, Theta, Theta_unique, Theta_inj). two_step_shift: zrow (Theta f) 2 = Theta (shift f), so the constrained double step is conjugate to the full one-sided shift on the free bits f (column -1 at odd times). Q01_iff_Theta: Q01 iff Theta f is never finitely supported. Q01_iff_bounded (BWR, by compactness): for every depth d there is B with a black cell of Theta f in [d,d+B) for every f. Q01_iff_staged. count_constrained: exactly 2^floor(W/2) starts of width <= W satisfy the constraint at every even step t <= W-1. Theta is triangular with a pivot at every even depth. backward_det, back_fin_iff (exact finite-preimage criterion), survive_iff and no_two_white (forced skeleton).
forms: period-2 exclusion (word 01) through Q01 and the faithful coupled CQ01
uniform Pi-1 strengthening: every finite ZBL row of width W violates the constraint by time 2W+8 (checked for W <= 71 by four C codes, W <= 56 in Lean)
techniques.core_idea: Under the period-2 hypothesis the only freedom is one bit per two steps, and left-permutive reconstruction turns any free-bit sequence f into a unique, usually infinite, initial row Theta(f). So the hypothetical counterexamples form a Cantor set homeomorphic to {0,1}^N on which the dynamics is the shift, and period 2 is excluded iff no point of this set is a finite row.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This is an exact 'solve the system' description of all hypothetical counterexamples, the analogue of Cloitre's parity split for Q-tilde. What is missing is any finite description of Theta: beyond depth about 15 there are only the affine identities L1=1, L2+L3=1, L2+L5=1 (to depth 33), no finite transducer (Myhill-Nerode classes grow about 1.79^s), no self-similarity under 10 transforms, ANF degree about k/2, and Theta of a random f is statistically i.i.d. Barrier check: the Q01-only barriers apply; their truncated-stripe witnesses have f close to 1^inf, which violates the right half's proven no-11111 law, so CQ01 escapes them, but the two-sided JointBarrier (ether truncations) still blocks local two-sided rankings.
techniques.obstacle: BWR, or D(W) <= 2W+8 for all W, is a uniform pseudo-randomness statement about Theta; the random-constraint model predicts D(W) about 1.82W and matches the measured survival to 0.2%.
techniques.artifacts: Lean: Rule30ZeroBoundary.lean (Theta, two_step_shift, Q01_iff_Theta, Q01_iff_bounded, Q01_iff_staged, count_constrained, edge_region_barrier, jen_clock, free_bits_no00_no11111), Rule30PeriodTwoCoupled.lean; originals research/progA-backdet/lean/ZBLCore.lean, research/A-reconmap/lean/ZBL.lean, research/A-monovariant/lean/ZBL.lean; verifier supplements research/verify-A1reform-rigor/A1Reform.lean and research/verify-A2-reconmap-rigor/ZBLcheck.lean. D(W) and forced-window tables: research/A-reconmap/c/zt2.c and the dfs.c programs. No license file.

techniques.name: Epochs of constrained ZBL histories, stripe stability and absorption, and the deviation-front odometer
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize round 2 (agents q01-monovariant, q01-reconstruction, q01-invariants; verifier V-A2-epochs-rigor) and final batch (kernel-certify-r2, target 2). Modules Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripe, Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeFront, Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeFamily. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Found by Claude Code agents; the round-2 synthesis agent noticed that one agent's stripe-absorption theorem proves another agent's open conjecture A8 (now Theta_eventually_stripe_iff); a verifier corrected the phase convention of the epoch bridge; the final-batch agent kernel-checked the stripe-prefix family.
techniques.proved: Epochs (Lean; first_defect_phase is the phase-free form): the first deviation from the stripe ...10101 moves exactly one cell toward the wall per step; in a surviving history it sits at depth d with t+d even; f_s = 0 exactly at a reset; a history dies exactly when an epoch has odd length. stripe_absorb / stripe2_absorb: a row equal to the stripe beyond an odd (even) depth becomes exactly the stripe (the 2-cycle 11(01)^inf <-> (01)^inf), via a front lemma checked by decide over 2^12-2^13 windows. Theta_eventually_stripe_iff: Theta(f) is eventually the stripe iff f is eventually 1. stripe_prefix_family_list: S[1..m]v0^inf with |v| <= 3 dies by time d-1+31 (front_sound plus 8 purely periodic window cycles of lengths 4096-65536). Computer only: |v| <= 7 dies by m+53; for v = 1 the extra survival depends only on m mod 2^13, with values 1, 3, 5, ... at frequencies 2^-1, 2^-2, ....
forms: period-2 exclusion (Q01) on special classes of rows: stripe-tailed and near-stripe starts
techniques.core_idea: Always-black columns saturate the OR and block outward information, so a stripe background confines and absorbs perturbations. Behind the moving first deviation the cells obey the right-diagonal recurrence, so a perturbation of the stripe is governed by a finite 2-adic odometer.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: The epoch decomposition is formally the closest analogue of Q-tilde's arches: epochs tile the time axis and a history dies iff an epoch has odd length; under the empirical block law every epoch depth would lie in {6, 10}. A Q-tilde-style proof would need an exact epoch map (row at a reset to next epoch length) with a finite description; round 2 proposed building it on Rule30RightPeriods and nobody did. Barrier check: the near-stripe results escape the Q01-only barriers only because they cover a thin special class; the actual onset background is white, which has no walls (the edge escapes at speed 1).
techniques.obstacle: One zero in f gives a bounded defect packet (depths [2a+2, 2a+14]), but two zeros already interact over depths [12, 84]; front-window orbits grow like 2^(0.43J), so family certificates do not scale (|v| = 8 already has tails surviving at least 62 steps after arrival).
techniques.artifacts: Lean: Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripe.lean, Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeFront.lean (front_sound, family_of_class), Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeFamily.lean, Rule30Certificates/ZeroBoundaryStripeCycles0-2.lean; research/V-A2-epochs-rigor/Supp.lean. Code: research/A-invsearch/front_cert.c and front_family.c, research/A-monovariant/family.c, research/kernel-certify-r2/t2 (orbits.c, certs.py). No license file.

techniques.name: Bit-sliced kernel checkers and packed-Nat certificates in core Lean
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize final batch (agent kernel-certify-r2, adversarially verified) and round-1 window certificates; modules Rule30ZeroBoundaryLanes, Rule30ZeroBoundaryWidth52, Rule30FactorWindow, Rule30Window; builds on the kernel-decide cost model learned in the ruliology catalog work of 2026-10-10. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: A Claude Code agent replaced a per-path kernel DFS (about 0.04 ms per node) by a bit-sliced lane checker and proved its soundness; a verifier agent rebuilt all 109 source files from scratch into its own build directory and checked tightness (the check fails with K = D(W)).
techniques.proved: q01_of_checks / q01_of_chunks (soundness): if every chunk check passes, every ZBL start of width <= W violates the Q01 constraint at an even time < K. One Nat holds 2^18 lanes (one per choice of the first 18 free bits); anti-diagonals come from a running XOR (scanN) proved equal to the catalog's reconstruction. q01_width_le_52 (bound 96 = D(52), 256 chunks, about 80 s, in the catalog) and q01_width_le_56 (1024 chunks, about 345 s, archive only). Same style: transient_add_period_ge (all 16,359 length-26 windows of c(0..16383) are distinct, by a sorted permutation plus a coverage bitmap, so T+P >= 16359) and no_small_eventual_period (no P <= 4096 with T <= 8192, from 16,384 kernel-computed center bits).
forms: Morse-Hedlund / factor-complexity form on a finite prefix
finite windows of (T, P) for the base and base-B forms
techniques.core_idea: Run exhaustive searches inside the Lean kernel with GMP-accelerated Nat bit operations: pack 2^18 search branches into one natural number, update them with shifts and AND/OR/XOR, and split the remaining branches into separate chunk theorems. A general soundness theorem links the bit program to the mathematical definitions, so the kernel is the only trusted base (no native_decide, no bv_decide).
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Infrastructure for any future argument that needs finite base cases (Q-tilde's proof itself needs RA/RB for m <= 10 by decide +kernel) or finite per-level identities. Ready extensions: Q01 at W = 58 (about 2048 chunks, 14 min), the period-3 death tables (Q001, C3s001, C3w(011)), chunked width-14 period-2 language certificates. Barrier check: finite checks never settle an all-W or all-transient statement; finite rows of radius w fake periodic prefixes for about 1.25w-1.9w steps (round-1 faking horizons).
techniques.obstacle: Cost doubles with every +2 in W, and no finite computation proves Q01 without a uniform argument.
techniques.artifacts: Lean: Rule30ZeroBoundaryLanes.lean, Rule30ZeroBoundaryWidth52.lean, Rule30Certificates/ZeroBoundaryWidth52Chunks0-3.lean, Rule30FactorWindow.lean, Rule30Window.lean; W <= 56: research/kernel-certify-r2/t1 (buildall56.sh, 64 chunk files, about 6 min at about 1.5 GB each), lanes.py (Python lane model), nodes.c. No license file.

techniques.name: Barrier theorems: what any proof of Problem 1 must use
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize rounds 1-2 and final batch (agents complexity, algebraic, new-ideas, absorbing-left, q01-invariants, q01-monovariant, q01-backward, p4-edge, p4-nested-scc, kernel-certify-r2). Modules Rule30Realization, Rule30ZeroBoundaryBarriers, Rule30ZeroBoundary (edge_region_barrier), Rule30DrivenLeft (barrier_exists, barrier_unique), Rule30EtherTrap (word_lemma). People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Each barrier was produced by a Claude Code agent whose attack failed and which then proved why; verifiers delimited the scope (e.g. the truncated-stripe barriers bar Q01-only proofs, not CQ01).
techniques.proved: (1) Rule30Realization.barrier (Lean): rules 90, 150, 210 (new = left XOR g(center,right), g(0,0)=0, g(0,1)=1) satisfy Jen's adjacent-column theorem and share the 2-power right-diagonal periods and odometer, yet their single-seed centers are eventually constant. (2) column_realizable_unique (Lean): for every right half and every target column there is exactly one configuration, so every eventually periodic column is realized by an infinite configuration. (3) Q01-only (Lean): finite_abstraction_has_lasso, no_local_ranking (width + wall window + edge window), no_edge_dfa_ranking (any DFA reading from the edge). (4) no_joint_local_ranking (Lean): for rule 30 on Z from arbitrary finite configurations, no ranking of (leftmost black, rightmost black, center window, both edge windows) decreases at every flip of the center. (5) edge_region_barrier (Lean): any far part, with all its left-edge structure, can be completed near the wall so that column -1 follows any prescribed values before time d. (6) barrier_exists/barrier_unique (Lean): left starts with leftmost black cell at -n correspond bijectively to column -1 on steps 0..n-2. (7) Additive barrier (paper proof plus certified modular ranks, not Lean): rule 30 squared has no nontrivial additive conservation law of range <= 8 over Q or <= 9 mod 2 (ordinary to range 12, alternating to 10). (8) Local obstruction for strip certificates on words of length 2-7 (computer; Lean word_lemma for the pure ether at width <= 20). (9) Trap-avoiding strip paths have the full growth rate (computer).
forms: especially the 2-adic, automatic/Christol and F2-algebraic forms: the 90/150/210 barrier shows that F2-linear, Lucas, odometer and automaticity arguments are shared with rules whose centers are eventually constant
techniques.core_idea: Each barrier exhibits objects that satisfy everything a proof class can see while the conclusion fails: rules 90, 150, 210; infinite realizers of any periodic column; truncated stripes that survive n steps; ether truncations whose center alternates for about 7N steps; far parts that can be completed near the wall at will.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: These are the filters to run on every external technique in the portfolio before investing in it. A valid argument for any equivalent form must (i) use the OR of rule 30, since it fails for 90/150/210; (ii) use the finiteness of the configuration, by realization; (iii) be non-local in space, by the local, finite-state, edge-DFA and additive barriers; (iv) not rest on edge structure plus windows shorter than the wall-to-structure distance. Methods that work for linear or automatic sequences (Christol, Lucas, Mahler, 2-adic odometers, ANF degree) can only be components.
techniques.obstacle: Barriers are scope-limited, which is also where hope lies: the Q01-only barriers do not cover CQ01, and nothing excludes arguments that combine the right edge's global 2-adic structure with bulk information, or that use single-seed-specific facts beyond the two edges.
techniques.artifacts: Lean: Rule30Realization.lean (realize, unique, column_realizable_unique, seed_perturbation, barrier, center90, center150, center210), Rule30ZeroBoundaryBarriers.lean, Rule30ZeroBoundary.lean, Rule30DrivenLeft.lean, Rule30EtherTrap.lean; research/verify-A2-rigor/ZBLBarrierCorollary.lean; research/A-invsearch/lean/{ZBLBarrier,JointBarrier,ZBLEdgeDFA}.lean. Additive barrier code: research/A-invsearch/conslaw*.py. No license file.

techniques.name: Jen with a clock (quantitative, finite-window Jen) and its right-half interface
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize round 2 (agent q01-backward; also proved by q01-monovariant and q01-reconstruction). The same lemma appears as 'Theorem A' in the third-party ghywel/placego notes, which were not re-run. Module Rule30ZeroBoundary. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Formalized by Claude Code agents in round 2; re-compiled by the synthesis agent; the link to linear-complexity profiles below is an observation made in this inventory, not an archive result.
techniques.proved: jen_clock (Lean; propext, Quot.sound, re-checked 2026-10-15): if column -1 of a finite ZBL row whose last black cell is at depth m is P-periodic on [T, T+l], then l+2 <= T+m+2P. free_bits_clock: a p-periodic stretch [s0, s0+l] of the free bits has 2l+2 <= 2s0+m+4p, so Q01 holds for every eventually periodic f and every f with a long periodic window. alternating_right_col1_clock / alternating_free_bits_clock: if the center alternates from T, column 1 (and column -1) at the white times has no p-periodic window [k0, k0+l] with 2l+2 > 2k0+T+1+4p.
forms: period-2 exclusion through a finitary right-half statement
effective strengthenings of the F2 linear-complexity form and of the base-B irrationality form (see transfer)
techniques.core_idea: Jen's argument with time made explicit: the left edge advances one cell per step, so a periodic window of length about T+m+2P in one column already forces a contradiction. It needs only a finite periodic window, so a finitary right-half statement can feed it.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: Shape match: a P-periodic window [T, T+l] of a sequence s means its prefix of length T+l+1 is generated by an LFSR of length T+P (feedback s_t = s_(t-P)), so a linear-complexity profile L(n) >= n/2 - K forces l <= T+2P+2K-1, the jen_clock inequality with 2K in place of m. Berlekamp-Massey data for c give |L_c(n) - n/2| <= 9.5 for n <= 10^6 (round-1 data, not Lean), the behaviour of a random sequence. So a clocked Jen for c itself is the periodic-feedback case of a near-perfect linear-complexity profile, an effective strengthening of the F2 form, and the same windows give irrationality-exponent bounds for denominators 2^T(2^P-1). Barrier check: the clock form is not OR-specific (Jen holds for 90/150/210), so it can only be the finishing step.
techniques.obstacle: The interface needs column 1 at white times to have a periodic window longer than k0 + T/2 + 2p, i.e. zero-entropy right-half output for linear time. The true output under period-2 driving has positive entropy (p(128) about 1.6-2.1x10^4), so clock windows and Sturmian-type exclusions cannot reach the real case.

techniques.name: Hidden slowness and exact-fit interleaving: machine-checked totality of the Mantovanelli-Hofstadter sequence Q-tilde (OEIS A394051)
techniques.origin: Own project VibeProof/HofstadterQ/lean (Lake package qtilde), Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code, commits d679e2e, 61b64a1, 6bf26d8 on 2026-10-15, formalizing sections 2-3 of B. Cloitre, 'The Mantovanelli-Hofstadter Sequence', arXiv:2604.06237 (v1 2026-04-04, v3 2026-07-22). Recursion introduced by M. Mantovanelli (arXiv:2603.16111); independent computer-assisted proof by Mantovanelli, arXiv:2603.29622 (v1 2026-03-31, v3 2026-07-22, Python certificate on Zenodo).
techniques.ai_involvement: Cloitre's v3 PDF declares that he used OpenAI ChatGPT 5.5 and 5.6 'to assist with language editing, manuscript organization, and exploratory computations' (the abstract page has no such statement). Mantovanelli's v3 declares ChatGPT use for language editing, bibliographic organization, LaTeX assistance and exploratory calculations, and says the result 'is not claimed to be formalized in Lean, Coq, Isabelle, or HOL'. Our Lean proof was written with Claude Code (Anthropic) in one session.
techniques.proved: QTilde.qtilde_wellDefined: there is Q with IsQTilde Q (Q(1)=Q(2)=1, the recursion holds for n >= 3 and every recursive argument lies in [1, n-1]); isQTilde_unique; Qt_bounds: 1 <= Q-tilde(n) <= n. Core Lean 4.30, no Mathlib, 1,436 lines, about 10 s to build; #print axioms re-run 2026-10-15: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Simplification over the paper: Cloitre's Dyck-height invariants are not needed; each RA/RB case on an arch is the shuffle-count identity pre_count at the two heads of the interleaving machine plus a parked-head lemma. Cloitre's paper is an unrefereed preprint; Mantovanelli's v3, section 12, says his v2 finite-state closure 'left a semantic gap: closure of the abstract overlap graph did not imply that every future recurrence position realized the required source context'.
forms: methodological: word/automatic (Christol) forms, the period-2 left problem (Theta plays the role of the parity split), discrepancy/height descriptions of the right-half output
techniques.core_idea: The (-1)^n term makes every value odd, so each parity class a(m), b(m) is slow (increments 0 or 1), and their difference is a walk of positive and negative arches, each encoded by a binary word. The arch words are generated level by level by two exact-fit interleaving laws (P0 = 001011; N_r = Interleave(P_r[2:], P_r[:-1], 1); P_(r+1) = Interleave(00 N_r 1, 0 N_r, 0); a_(r+1) = 4a_r - 1). Totality becomes 'the two-tape machine never reads an exhausted tape', one finite identity per level, proved by induction.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: The pattern to transfer: find coordinates in which the only freedom is binary and is generated by finitely many deterministic laws per level, then prove the constraint as an exact-fit identity. Rule 30 has the binary coordinates (Theta and the free bits f for period 2; skeleton free bits for periods 3 and 4) but no laws: Theta is pseudo-random beyond depth about 15, and every constrained system the archive measured has positive entropy (left free bits: full shift; period-2 right output about 0.07 bits per white time; period-4 free bits 1.27-1.32 per period), whereas Q-tilde's arch words are deterministic. Barrier check: Mantovanelli's finite-state gap is the phenomenon formalized by our finite_abstraction_has_lasso and the trap-relaxation results; for Q01 every sound finite abstraction has a surviving lasso, so a Mantovanelli-style finite-state certificate cannot exist.
techniques.obstacle: Zero entropy made Q-tilde provable. Rule 30's constrained systems have positive entropy everywhere except in boundary layers (right edge, stripe backgrounds, ethers), and there Q-tilde-style exact descriptions already exist in the archive (RightPeriods, stripe_absorb, front_sound).
techniques.artifacts: VibeProof/HofstadterQ/lean/QTilde/{Basic, Interleave, Arches, Slow, Recurrence, Totality}.lean: a reusable two-tape interleaving-machine library (head formulas head_i_eq/head_j_eq, exact-fit criterion fits_of_inv, shuffle counts pre_count/pre_ht, parked heads parked_X/parked_Y, count_interleave) usable to machine-check any proposed morphic or interleaving description, e.g. of the 10000/100 right-half output. Prior-art report: VibeProof/HofstadterQ/reports/Hofstadter Q formalization prior art.md. Public on github.com/sw1sh/vibe-proof (origin/main), no license file.

techniques.name: Period-2 right-half block law: column 1 at white times lies in {10000, 100}*, 100 isolated, density 3/14
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize round-2 synthesis measurement (research/synth-r2/rc3.c, rc4.c, rc5.c, y_out.txt), cross-validated by an independent Python code in the write-up phase (writeup-r2/yindep.py); coordinator search period2/search_lang.py; partial Lean laws from the final batch (kernel-certify-r2 t4). Re-analysed in this inventory. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Found by the round-2 Claude Code synthesis agent while measuring the right half; re-implemented by the write-up agent; statistics re-analysed in this inventory (Claude Code, 2026-10-15).
techniques.proved: Lean, partial: under an alternating center the free bits eventually avoid 00, 11111, 011010 and 01101110 (Rule30PeriodTwoWidth5.free_bit_constraints) and nine column-1 words at width 6, so a gap of 3 is eventually never followed by a gap of 2 or 4. Empirical (two independent codes, six runs on true and random finite right halves): after at most 27 samples every gap between ones of y is 3 or 5, so y is a concatenation of 100 and 10000 with 100 isolated; density 0.2136-0.2149 (3/14 = 0.21429); p(32)=92, p(64)=702, p(128)=15,960. The law is not strip-local: the strip relaxation admits gaps 2 and 4 at every width <= 12. Re-analysis here of y_out.txt (97,997 samples after the transient): runs of 10000 between consecutive 100s have length 3 (60%), 5 (12%), then 7, 9, 10, 11, ... up to 31, mean 4.98, giving density 3/14 within about +-0.00015; the run sequence carries about 2 bits per 100-block; the variance of the ones count in non-overlapping windows grows with local exponent 0.6-0.75 below about 450 samples and about 1 above, at about 2% of the i.i.d. Bernoulli(3/14) variance. So the archive's 'sub-diffusive discrepancy' holds only at short scales: the law is locally rigid but globally a random renewal process, not a balanced, rotation-like word (single run; few windows at the largest scales).
forms: period-2 exclusion (coupled CQ01): the law would restrict the free bits to {011, 01111}^inf and every epoch depth to {6, 10}
techniques.core_idea: Driven by 0101..., the right half next to the center runs like a 10-step wheel (block 10000) with occasional isolated short blocks 100. Under a real period 2 the free bits of the left half must be the complement of this output, so the law would hand the left problem a tiny language.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: This is the archive's one Q-tilde-like 'secret slowness': a two-letter code with a rigid local grammar, as Q-tilde's increments are binary. A proof for every finite right half, or of any law bounding epoch depths, would cut the coupled period-2 problem to a left problem of about 0.07 bits per white time; the coordinator's search under the law killed every left start of width <= 196, with survivors growing about 1.05x per unit of width (output not saved, so unverified). Barrier check: the law does not follow from any narrow strip, so, like Absorption, its proof must use the finiteness of the right half; its positive entropy means clock-window and Sturmian-type exclusions cannot finish the argument.
techniques.obstacle: Positive entropy remains after the law, and the 100-insertions behave like a random renewal process at large scales, so there is no hierarchy to exploit; a proof would itself be an ergodic or nucleation theorem for a chaotic driven half-line.
techniques.artifacts: Code and data: research/synth-r2/{rc3.c, rc4.c, rc5.c, rightcomplex.c, y_out.txt}, research/writeup-r2/{yindep.py, blocklaw_strip.py}, research/period2/search_lang.py; Lean: Rule30PeriodTwoWidth5.lean, Rule30PeriodTwoWidth6.lean, Rule30PeriodTwoLanguage.lean.
