techniques.name: Right-diagonal 2-power period theory and the right-edge 2-adic odometer
techniques.origin: Own project: Rule 30 Prize, module Rule30Diagonals (start of the attempt) and round 1 (agents diagonals, algebraic, with verifiers), module Rule30RightPeriods. Reproves and extends E. S. Rowland, 'Local Nested Structure in Rule 30', Complex Systems 16(3) (2006) 239-258. People: Nikolay Murzin with Claude Code agents.
techniques.ai_involvement: Structure theory found and proved in Lean by a Claude Code agent; a guessed lower bound (e_j >= floor(j/2)) was refuted by the same agent with kernel-checked counterexamples (e_14 <= 6, e_23 <= 8).
techniques.proved: e_step: e_(j+1) = e_j + R_(j+1)(2^(e_j)); the period doubles exactly when that cell is black, and the diagonal is then complemented by half its period. rows_at_powers_of_two: R_0..R_n have period 2^k iff row 2^k has n white cells left of its edge; row N = 2^k u reads 1 0^(J_k) 1 from the edge (J_0..J_37 computed, extending e_j to j = 85). restart: cell(N+s, N+q) = cell(s, q) when 0 <= s-q <= J_(nu2(N)), so column 2^k u repeats c(0..J_k). center_black_lt: c(t) = 1 implies 2^(e_t) > t. no_three: the period never doubles three times in a row. log2(j+2)-1 <= e_j <= (2j+1)/3. On paper only: the right-edge orbit closure is conjugate to the 2-adic odometer, and L_j = 2^(e_j - 1) + 1 at each period jump (Lucas/Mahler).
forms: 2-adic irrationality and automatic/Christol forms, in vocabulary only (barred, see transfer)
computational irreducibility (Problem 3) through the restart copies
techniques.core_idea: In right-edge coordinates rule 30 is a triangular isometry of {0,1}^N; diagonal j+1 is driven by R_(j-1) OR R_(j-2) through an accumulator, so periods are powers of two and double by an explicit rule. It is an exact hierarchy, like Q-tilde's levels.
techniques.transfer_to_rule30: It is the most Q-tilde-like exact hierarchy in the archive, but it is thin: it controls about 2.3 log2 t diagonals at the right edge, c(t) lies in the first period of its diagonal whenever c(t) = 1, and the restart copies of c have logarithmic length. The deviation-front odometer of the stripe-prefix families is the same structure moved to the front. Empirically right-half absorption favours periods 4 and 8, but 0101 rarely absorbs and 001 does, so the 2-power pattern is not a law. Barrier check: rules 60, 90, 150 and 210 share the whole structure, so it cannot decide Problem 1 or its 2-adic and automatic forms alone; it could be the exact right-edge component of a two-sided argument, the one combination no barrier excludes.
techniques.obstacle: The edge hierarchy never reaches the center, and periodic drivers leave the tail periods growing (no diagonal signature of a periodic center). The open side conjectures (J_E < 2^E; liminf e_j / j > 0) would be new rule-30 theorems but not steps toward Problem 1.

surveys.notes:
AREA: inventory of proof techniques from our own AI-assisted projects: VibeProof/Rule30Prize (2026-10-15, Claude Code multi-agent attempt) and VibeProof/HofstadterQ (Q-tilde totality, machine-checked 2026-10-15). Nothing was posted, committed or edited in the user's repos; the parent task list was not touched.

1. SOURCES READ: Rule30Prize/README.md, lean/README.md, research/results/round1.json, round2.json, final-batch.json (every agent's structured output, including all syntheses and verifiers), writeup/rule30-state.html (sections 4, 6.4, 8, 10), research/period2/NOTES.md; HofstadterQ/lean/QTilde/*.lean and reports/Hofstadter Q formalization prior art.md.

2. CHECKS RUN IN THIS PASS (2026-10-15): #print axioms on 12 archive theorems (masked_jen, effective_boundary, problem1_iff_no_word, jen_clock, two_step_shift, Q01_iff_Theta, stripe_absorb, q01_width_le_52, no_joint_local_ranking, least_period_four_of_absorption, Rule30Realization.barrier, no_eventual_period_two_of_CQ01) and on 3 Q-tilde theorems (qtilde_wellDefined, isQTilde_unique, Qt_bounds): only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Every other cited Lean name and research path was located by grep/ls. One path fix: round 1 calls generalize-jen's scanner strip_scc.c, but the archive holds scc_scan.py and strip_scan.py.

3. VERDICT: no technique from our projects proves Problem 1, any equivalent form, or any full period >= 2. Every open statement (Q01/CQ01, Absorption(w), AbsorptionT(t001), C3(w), Q001, C3s001, C3w(011), D(W) <= 2W+8) has the same shape: every orbit of a positive-entropy constrained system eventually violates a constraint or nucleates a wall. Worth salvaging:
(a) the Lean interface any new idea must hit: masked_jen, effective_step, problem1_iff_no_word, column_realizable_unique, Q01/CQ01, Absorption, C3;
(b) the barrier filters;
(c) the kernel-certificate infrastructure;
(d) the two robust but unexplained phenomena: period-4 and 001 absorption, and the period-2 block law.

4. MAPPING TO THE LIBRARY'S FORMS: nearly everything acts on the per-word decomposition (problem1_iff_no_word), period by period. Direct contacts:
- Morse-Hedlund: Rule30FactorWindow (T+P >= 16359).
- F2 / linear complexity: Berlekamp-Massey data (|L_c(n) - n/2| <= 9.5 up to 10^6, not in Lean), and the jen_clock shape. My observation here: a P-periodic window [T,T+l] has linear complexity <= T+P, so a near-perfect profile gives l <= T+2P+O(1), which is the clocked-Jen inequality. The same windows give irrationality-exponent bounds for denominators 2^T(2^P-1).
- Rules 86/135/149: the archive's white-seed theorem concerns rule 135 from a BLACK seed (column -1). Symmetry.lean correctly treats that as a different question.
- 2-adic and Christol forms: touched only through the right-edge odometer and 2-kernel data, and both are barred by rules 90/150/210.
- Q-rationality / natural boundary, normality (Problem 2) and irreducibility (Problem 3): no archive technique touches these beyond window data and the paper-only ANF-degree result.

5. WHAT Q-TILDE TEACHES, AND THE HIDDEN-STRUCTURE QUESTION: Q-tilde became provable because (-1)^n makes every value odd, so each parity class is slow. The sequence is then generated deterministically, level by level, by two exact-fit interleaving laws, and totality is one finite identity per level. Our Lean proof needs only shuffle counts at the machine heads plus a parked-head lemma, not Cloitre's Dyck heights. A proof of Problem 1 goes by contradiction, so the matching move is to show that periodicity forces hidden regular structure that finiteness forbids. The archive points to four candidates:
(i) The 2-power right-diagonal hierarchy and the deviation-front odometer. They are exact and hierarchical like Q-tilde's levels, but only O(log t) diagonals wide. They never reach c (center_black_lt), and rules 90/150/210 share them.
(ii) Ethers and walls. For 0001/0011/0111 and 001 the true right half empirically always settles into one; this is the closest analogue of a hidden-structure theorem. For 0101 it happens in about 3% of runs, and for 011 never.
(iii) The period-2 block law. It is Q-tilde-like at the alphabet level: two letters with a rigid local grammar. But my re-analysis of the archived 98k-sample run shows a positive-entropy renewal process: about 2 bits per 100-block, and window-count variance that is diffusive above about 450 samples, at about 2% of the i.i.d. variance. It is sub-diffusive only at short scales, so there is no hierarchy, and the archive's 'sub-diffusive discrepancy' wording should be limited to short scales (one run, few windows at large scales).
(iv) Epochs. They are formally the analogue of Q-tilde's arches: a history dies iff an epoch has odd length. But the epoch map has no finite description: two resets interact over unbounded depth, and Theta has about 1.79^s Myhill-Nerode classes.
Conclusion: none of the constrained systems the archive measured shows a zero-entropy hidden structure. Q-tilde's method transfers only to the boundary layers, where the archive already used it (RightPeriods, stripe_absorb, front_sound).

6. SUGGESTED USE FOR THE PORTFOLIO:
- Run every external technique through the filters first: does it use the OR, use finiteness, and work non-locally, rather than resting on edge structure plus short windows?
- Aim partial results at Absorption(0111) (single alignment, no skeleton, delays <= 829), and at a proof of the block law or of any bound on epoch depths for every finite right half.
- A bounded Q-tilde-style probe: measure the Myhill-Nerode growth of the epoch map restricted to the block-law language, and stop if it grows exponentially.

# Rule 30, Problem 1: portfolio of proof techniques produced 2024–2026

*Compiled 2026-10-15 for the equivalents library (`VibeProof/Rule30Prize/equivalents`, Lean 4.30.0 with Mathlib `c5ea003`). It merges six surveys (Rule 30 projects; irrationality and transcendence; words and automata; dynamics and non-periodicity; frontier-AI mathematics; our own archive), removes duplicates, checks each technique against our barrier theorems, and adds checks run for this portfolio (Appendix B). Downloaded third-party code was read but never executed.*

---

## 0. Conventions

**Glossary**
- **c(t)**: the centre column of rule 30 (new cell = l ⊕ (c ∨ r)) started from one black cell: 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, … (OEIS A051023). Problem 1 says c is not eventually periodic.
- **Eventual period word w**: a word with c = w^∞ from some time on. `problem1_iff_no_word` states Problem 1 ⇔ no nonempty word is one. *Black* and *white times* are the times where the hypothesised tail reads 1 and 0.
- **Effective boundary**: the left half sees column 0 only through c(t) ∧ c(t+1) (`effective_step`).
- **ZBL and Q01**: the ZBL is the zero-driven left half: rule 30 on the columns left of 0, with column 0 held white. Q01 says every finitely supported ZBL start eventually has column −1 white at an even step; it implies there is no eventual period 2. **CQ01** is the coupled version, faithful to the problem, in which both halves are finite.
- **Θ(f)**: the unique ZBL start whose column −1 at the white times reads f. Q01 ⇔ Θ(f) is never finitely supported.
- **u**: column 1 read at the white times beside a 0101 centre. Under period 2, u = ¬f (`p1_odd`).
- **Light-cone language, MFW**: the light-cone language is the set of length-L words u₀…u_{L−1} that some right window of width 2L−1 produces. A *minimal forbidden word* (MFW) is absent from it while its prefix and its suffix are present.
- **Absorption(w)**: every finite right half driven by w^∞ eventually enters a closed, consistently labelled trap.
- **Ether, wall**: an ether is a rule-30 pattern, periodic in space and time, whose columns carry candidate period words. A wall is a set of strip states that is closed under every far input.

**Status labels.** These record what was actually checked, not what was announced.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Lean (ours)** | In our catalog or library, with axioms re-printed: only `propext`, `Quot.sound`, `Classical.choice`. |
| **Formal (3rd party)** | Machine-checked by its authors; **not rebuilt by us**. |
| **Peer-reviewed** | Journal or refereed conference. |
| **Preprint** | arXiv, Zenodo or repository write-up. The card says what we reproduced. |
| **Computed** | A finite computation: evidence, not proof. |
| **Derived here** | An argument first written in this portfolio; not machine-checked. |
| **Announced** | A claim without a checkable artifact. |
| **Refuted** | Shown to be wrong. |

**Promise** rates how much a technique can contribute to *proving* Problem 1 or an equivalent form: high, medium, low or none. When a technique mainly adds library entries or infrastructure, the card rates that separately. **Nothing in this portfolio rates high.**

**Barriers used as filters.** These come from our archive and are Lean theorems unless marked otherwise.
- **F-OR**: rules 90, 150 and 210 share Jen's theorem, the light-cone edge, the power-of-two right-diagonal periods and the odometer, yet their single-seed centres are eventually constant (`Rule30Realization.barrier`). A valid argument must therefore use rule 30's OR.
- **F-FIN**: every column, paired with every right half, is realised by exactly one configuration, which is usually infinite (`column_realizable_unique`). A valid argument must therefore use finiteness.
- **B1, B6**: no finite abstraction, and no automaton reading from the edge, gives a ranking for Q01 (`finite_abstraction_has_lasso`, `no_edge_dfa_ranking`). The witnesses are truncated stripes.
- **B2, JointBarrier**: no function of (width, wall window, edge window) decreases along every surviving double step (`no_local_ranking`). In the two-sided setting, no function of (outermost black positions, centre window, edge windows) decreases at every flip of the centre (`no_joint_local_ranking`). The witnesses are truncations of c7, a rule-30 orbit of temporal period 4 whose centre alternates.
- **C6** (computed): no nontrivial additive conservation law exists for rule 30 up to range 10, or for rule 30² up to range 8.
- **B7** (derived here; card D8): no additive ranking of range ≤ 8 certifies Q01.
- **Edge region**: edge structure, together with windows shorter than the distance to the wall, carries no information (`edge_region_barrier`).
- **Local obstruction** (computed; Lean `word_lemma` for the ether): no strip certificate exists for any primitive word of length 2–7 at width ≤ 16 (≤ 20 for 0001).

B1, B2 and B6 apply to Q01 only. Their witnesses have free bits starting with 11111, which a real period-2 tail forbids.

**Licenses.** "No LICENSE" means all rights are reserved: re-derive the code, or ask before copying it.

---

## 1. Orientation

### 1.1 Bottom line
- **No technique from 2024–2026, with or without AI, excludes any nonconstant eventual period of the single-seed centre column.**
  - Period 1 is settled for every nonzero finite configuration: Condrey, arXiv 2609.09431, with third-party Lean in rule30-foundry.
  - Period 2 is the next open case.
- **Every serious project stopped at the same wall**: every orbit of a positive-entropy constrained system must eventually violate a constraint. Each group words it differently:
  - placego: "no emptiness from a constrained side of positive entropy";
  - rule30-foundry: no transport bound from local u-bans to unbounded left weight;
  - Berzai: an interface language of positive entropy, which defeats every window size;
  - Fomin: a discrepancy problem for one orbit.

  placego (Claude, GPT, Kimi) halted on 2026-10-14; its swarm SW-01 judged 10 proposals and kept none.
- **Frontier provers have not reached this regime.**
  - AlphaProof Nexus failed on every irrationality or digit problem it attempted.
  - On FrontierMath Erdős the best model solved 2 of 68 curated open problems at $300.
  - In OEIS Open, every model failed the digit-randomness conjecture A214560.
- **What can be salvaged:**
  1. **Exact period-2 right-half laws** (rule30-foundry). This portfolio extended them to length 15 and fed them into the left search: they cut the excess survival of the left half from about 0.8W to about 0.19W (Appendix B).
  2. **Word-exclusion engines** for long words (Berzai, placego, ours). They complement each other.
  3. **CC0 Lean code for new equivalent forms** (Stephan): not P-recursive, not algebraic over ℚ(z), not rational over ℚ, Hankel determinants, 2-adic irrationality.
  4. **One global algebraic handle that passes the rule-90 firewall**: Duhamel decomposition with Cartier closure.
  5. **Tooling** for agents, certificates and verification.
- **New barrier B7** (derived here). Additive rankings cannot certify Q01 at small range. This covers translation-invariant pattern counts, potentials found by LP over pattern counts, BBB(4)-style counts and, heuristically, polynomial matrix interpretations. It downgrades the certificate classes that the dynamics survey ranked highest.

### 1.2 Technique families and the forms they reach

| Family | Main cards | Equivalent forms reached | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Word-exclusion engines: a finite over-approximation of the right half, then (masked) Jen | C1, F14 | per-word form; tails in the shift-orbit form | Unconditional for long words (length ≥ 8). Provably cannot reach periods 2–7. |
| Coupled and left-half reductions | D2, D3, F2, F3, F5, F11 | periods 2–4, word by word; constrained-system form | The frontier. Both sides have positive entropy. |
| Algebraic series methods | A1, A2, A7, B1–B4 | F₂ power series; linear complexity; rationality over ℚ; 2-adic; automatic/Christol | Equivalences are cheap. A proof needs an invariant taking infinitely many values, and nobody has one. |
| Arithmetic irrationality | A3–A6, A9 | base-B real; 2-adic; Hankel | Zero margin for 0/1 digits. Needs analytic or multiplicative structure that c lacks. |
| Dynamics certificates | D7–D11 | Q01, CQ01, Absorption, finite windows | Regular and additive classes are barred (B1, B6, B7). SAT only extends finite cases. |
| AI workflow patterns | E1–E9 | any Lean statement | Tooling; no mathematics of its own. |

### 1.3 One object, many names (deduplication map)

| Object | Our archive | placego | rule30-foundry | Berzai | Others |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Forced left half under period 2 | Θ(f); Q01 ⇔ LR ⇔ BWR; D(W) | LR, R(d), R_real(d) | completion(u,N), W_N, L1–L4 | – | Kim's inverse layers; Woffinden's thread; eliottcassidy THM-4048 |
| Column 1 at white times beside 0101 | u; block law; width-5/6 laws | visible column 1; "the wheel"; channel bound | u-language, 12 MFWs | interface language L(01) | – |
| Defect identity L_{t+p} ⊕ L_t = (1 ⊕ C_t)(R_{t+p} ⊕ R_t) | masked Jen, `effective_step` | – | – | interface identity | Condrey's time-shift defect; Kim; the transferred Antihydra argument |
| Rule 30 = rule 150 ⊕ (c ∧ r) | ANF note (paper) | – | forcing identity | Duhamel formula | – |
| Jen with a clock | `jen_clock` | Theorem A | – | – | – |
| Word exclusion by a finite right strip | strip and rank certificates | strip graphs, stable sets | – | K-window automaton | cochon123 |
| Period 1 for finite configurations | single-seed proof via Jen | entry 37 | 50 Lean declarations | – | Condrey |
| 2-adic presentation | right-edge odometer | §8.77 T-function | – | remark | wryan2986; Stephan's ℤ₂ digits |
| Kill records | barrier theorems | SW-01, §8.116 | CLAIM_LEDGER | 27-route closed table | Condrey's roundtable; Fomin's assaults; Howe's 12 routes |

### 1.4 How far AI claims hold up
- **Aletheia's Erdős sweep** (arXiv 2601.22401): of 200 graded answers, 63 were technically correct and 13 (6.5%) were meaningful. Eight of those 13 were found in or rediscovered from the literature; four were novel, and none is at paper level.
- **AlphaProof Nexus** solved 9 of 353 Erdős problems and 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures. It failed on #68, #243, #247, #251, #257, #264(ii), #267, #269, #1049 and #406.
- **Overclaims and errors:**
  - A GPT-5 "Erdős breakthrough" post was deleted in October 2025.
  - In First Proof batch 1, organisers confirmed 2 of 10 answers where 6 were claimed.
  - The formal-conjectures "solved" tag on A6697 covers only the generating-function algebra.
  - Statements were misformalised (#5226, A379240, #263).
  - cochon123's uniform Lemma F was wrong.
  - Mantovanelli's own v3 says his v2 finite-state closure "left a semantic gap".
  - Shallit's Cooper–Dutle paper had a gap in v1.
- **Kernel exploits:**
  - An AI-assisted "Collatz disproof" made Lean accept False through bug #14576 (fixed in 4.32.2, 2026-07-28).
  - Bug #14484 was found with GPT-5.6 Sol (fixed in 4.32.1).
  - Our library and catalog pin v4.30.0.
- **Rule 30 resolutions:** every claimed full resolution checked so far is invalid: Topal, Ulrey, azhar, Tan, Fradkin, Brauer, Basta, Deva, Das, and TLMC #1243.

---

## 2. Technique cards

### A. Irrationality and transcendence (base-B real, 2-adic, rationality over ℚ, natural boundary, transcendence)

#### A1. Stanley engine: P-recursive or algebraic with finitely many values ⇒ eventually periodic
*Promise: none as a route; high library value (three new forms). Status: Formal (3rd party), CC0, not rebuilt.*
- **Origin.** Ralf Stephan (IGDORE) with Claude Code.
  - Repository: [rwst/Ceiling-Orbits](https://github.com/rwst/Ceiling-Orbits), 2026-07-29 to 09-07. Stanley's closure property became a theorem instead of a cited axiom on 2026-09-06.
  - Paper: DOI [10.13140/RG.2.2.10727.82081](https://dx.doi.org/10.13140/RG.2.2.10727.82081).
  - Classical input: R. Stanley, Eur. J. Combin. 1 (1980).
- **AI.** Claude Code wrote the Lean under the author's review. The mathematics is elementary or classical.
- **Proved.**
  - `RB.eventuallyPeriodic_of_isPRecursive`: a finite-range w : ℕ → ℚ satisfying a nontrivial recurrence Σ_j Q_j(n)·w(n+j) = 0 is eventually periodic.
  - `eventuallyPeriodic_of_isAlgebraic_of_finite_coeffs`.
  - `Stanley.pRecursive_of_isAlgebraic`, over any field of characteristic 0.
  - The comparator configuration admits only the three standard axioms.
- **Idea.** Past some N, every window recurs infinitely often, so Σ_j Q_j(t)·w(m+j) is a polynomial in t with infinitely many roots. Its top coefficients give a recurrence with constant coefficients, which on a finite alphabet is a finite-state map. Stanley's step: ℚ(X)(f) is a finite extension closed under d/dX, so f, f′, …, f^(d) are linearly dependent.
- **Transfer.**
  - New equivalences: Problem 1 ⇔ c (as a map ℕ → ℚ) is not P-recursive ⇔ Σ c(t)zᵗ is not algebraic over ℚ(z) ⇔ it is not rational over ℚ.
  - It also proves, as a theorem, that holonomic tools (A9) cannot work on f = Σ c(t)zᵗ, because f is D-finite exactly when Problem 1 fails.
- **Obstacle.** These are equivalences only.
  - The code must be ported from v4.33.0-rc1 to our v4.30.0.
  - Mathlib `c5ea003` lacks `PowerSeries.coeff_iterate_derivative` (confirmed here).
  - Mathlib does have the `DifferentialAlgebra` instance for finite intermediate fields that Stanley's step needs.
- **Artifacts.** CC0: `RB/EventuallyPeriodic.lean` (~24 KB), `CITED/StanleyProof.lean` (~28 KB), `CITED/Stanley.lean`, `Challenge.lean`.

#### A2. 2-adic presentations
*Promise: low; medium library value. Status: Formal (3rd party) for the ℤ₂ digit lemma; preprint or computed for the rest.*
- **Origin.**
  - Stephan with Claude Code, [rwst/Transcendence-Criteria](https://github.com/rwst/Transcendence-Criteria), 2026-07-18 to 08-06: `B3.not_isEventuallyPeriodic_binaryDigit`, `B3.ratInt_eventuallyPeriodic_binaryDigit`.
  - Berzai's remark "the same object over ℤ₂" ([rule30-left-edge](https://github.com/nateberzai-svg/rule30-left-edge)).
  - placego RULE30-PRIZE.md §8.77, 2026-10-09 (Claude Cloud, with GPT audit GC814).
  - [wryan2986/rule30-lab](https://github.com/wryan2986/rule30-lab), July–August 2026, MIT.
  - Z. Chen and A. Winterhof, [arXiv 2504.09933](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.09933), 2025, no AI.
- **Proved.**
  - Lean: the digits of v ∈ ℤ₂ are eventually periodic ⇔ v ∈ ℚ.
  - In the frame of the right edge, R_{t+1} = R_t ⊕ (2R_t ∨ 4R_t) and c(t) = bit t of R_t (checked for t < 2000).
  - H(a) = a ⊕ (2a ∨ 4a) permutes ℤ/2^k for k ≤ 20. It is not ergodic, since H(0) = 0.
  - wryan2986: a unit-triangular isometry Δ with eventual periodicity ⇔ Δ(S) rational.
  - Chen–Winterhof: an algebraic 2-adic integer of degree d ≥ 2 has N-th 2-adic complexity ≥ N/d + O(1). A 2-adic algebraic and automatic sequence is eventually periodic.
- **Idea.** Read a row as a 2-adic integer. Rule 30 becomes a 1-Lipschitz T-function, and c(t) is digit t of Hᵗ(1).
- **Transfer.** New equivalences: Problem 1 ⇔ Σ c(t)2ᵗ ∈ ℤ₂ is irrational ⇔ the N-th 2-adic complexity of c is unbounded.
- **Obstacle.**
  - The diagonal read digit_t(Hᵗ(1)) is exactly what ergodic results do not control. They control fixed digits, that is fixed diagonals, which are all eventually periodic.
  - Rule 90 (multiplication by 1 + y²) has the same presentation and an eventually constant centre (F-OR).
  - When porting, do not import `BL/ConjugacyMap.lean` or `AB/StammeringSequences.lean`: both declare axioms. Run `#print axioms` afterwards.
- **Artifacts.** CC0 Lean (`B3/DigitPeriodicity.lean`, `BL/Basic.lean`). wryan2986 is MIT, Berzai MPL-2.0, placego has no LICENSE.

#### A3. Tail decay (Liouville, Erdős–Straus): reduction to unbounded runs
*Promise: low. Status: Formal (3rd party) for #1051; preprint for #258.*
- **Origin.**
  - [Erdős #1051](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1051): Aletheia, Google DeepMind's Gemini Deep Think agent. Solved in December 2025, made public on 2026-01-29/30; case study [arXiv 2601.22401](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22401).
  - Sharp generalisation by Barreto, Kang, Kim, Kovač and Zhang ([arXiv 2601.21442](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21442), accepted in Bull. LMS).
  - Lean proofs by [Seed-Prover 1.5](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Seed-Prover/blob/main/SeedProver-1.5/erdos_1051.lean), by Barreto, and in [LeanMarathon](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05400).
  - [Erdős #258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258): P. Chojecki with GPT-5.4 Pro (2026-04-14), using Theorem 1.1 of [Tao–Teräväinen](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01739).
- **AI.**
  - Aletheia found #1051 on its own. One of five graders objected to an unjustified "standard comparison theorems" step.
  - Humans proved the golden-ratio threshold.
  - GPT-5.4 noticed that an existing theorem already settles #258.
- **Proved.**
  - If a_n is strictly increasing and limsup a_n^(1/φⁿ) = ∞, then Σ 1/(a_n·a_{n+1}) is irrational. The threshold is sharp.
  - Σ τ(n)/(a₁⋯a_n) is irrational whenever a_n → ∞.
- **Idea.** If S = P/Q, then Q·D_N·(S − S_N) is a positive integer for every N. Fast growth pushes it below 1 along a subsequence.
- **Transfer.**
  - For x = Σ c(t)·2^(−t−1) = a/q, every white run followed by a black cell is shorter than log₂ q + 1. Since no column is eventually constant, "c has runs of unbounded length" implies Problem 1.
  - Data: the record runs in 10⁷ bits are 22 (white) and 23 (black), about log₂ n.
  - Dibujaron's Lean bounds point the other way: a black run starting at time a ≥ 1 is shorter than a, and a white run is shorter than 3a.
- **Obstacle.**
  - 0/1 digits decay exactly geometrically, so the Liouville margin is zero.
  - "Unbounded runs" is a rare-pattern statement about one orbit, strictly stronger than Problem 1: words like Thue–Morse are aperiodic with bounded runs.
- **Artifacts.** `erdos_1051.lean` (Apache-2.0), LeanMarathon (Apache-2.0), formal-conjectures `1051.lean` and `258.lean`.

#### A4. Conspiracy repulsion and prime-pattern lattices: a "Chowla for c" target
*Promise: low. Status: preprint (Tao–Teräväinen); Lean conditional on a conjecture (#251); announced (normality claims).*
- **Origin.**
  - T. Tao and J. Teräväinen, [arXiv 2512.01739](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01739) (v1 2025-12-01, v2 2026-04-25). The text is entirely human-written.
  - J. Land, Erdős #251, conditional on Kuperberg's uniform Hardy–Littlewood conjecture. The Lean was written by Gemini 3.8 Flash workers coordinated by Codex (2026-09-05/06; [beetree/math_erdos_251](https://github.com/beetree/math_erdos_251), no license).
  - Normality claims posted on 2026-09-07 are announcements only.
- **Proved.** Σ ω(n)/2ⁿ is irrational: Erdős #69, and #257 for the primes.
- **Idea.**
  - Rationality puts every tail on a lattice (1/Q)ℤ.
  - A dilation identity, ω(pn) = ω(n) + 1 − 1_{p|n}, together with alternating Gowers-cube sums, cancels the leading terms.
  - Correlation estimates then spread the remainder, which contradicts the lattice.
- **Transfer.**
  - The argument needs (i) a dilation identity for c and (ii) two-point decorrelation of c at every shift.
  - (ii) alone already implies Problem 1, since a period h forces correlation 1 at shift h.
  - So a "Chowla conjecture for c" is a natural target between Problems 1 and 2.
  - Note that Problem 2 (density ½) does not imply Problem 1, whereas full normality does.
- **Obstacle.**
  - c has neither ingredient.
  - Rule 90 does have the dilation identity cell(2t, 2i) = cell(t, i), and its centre is eventually constant (F-OR).
  - The correlation input is as hard as Problem 2.

#### A5. Window–residue rigidity with a growth ceiling (rational-base words)
*Promise: low. Status: Formal (3rd party), CC0, not rebuilt.*
- **Origin.**
  - Stephan with Claude Code, [arXiv 2609.19007](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19007) (v1 2026-07-18, v2 2026-09-17), in the Transcendence-Criteria and Ceiling-Orbits repositories.
  - Formalises Akiyama–Frougny–Sakarovitch (2008) and Dubickas (2009).
  - Context: J. Kopra, [arXiv 2202.13809](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13809) (TCS 2023).
- **Proved.**
  - The parity word of x_{n+1} = ⌈3x_n/2⌉ is not eventually periodic, and its factor complexity is ≥ ⌊41(m−1)/24⌋ + 1.
  - The same holds for every coprime p > q ≥ 2.
  - Irrationality of K(3) stays open.
- **Idea.**
  - A window of length m pins x_n modulo 2^m, so a repeated window costs a factor 2^k in |x_c − x_a|.
  - The state grows only like (3/2)^c, and log₂(3/2) < 1, so long repetitions are impossible.
- **Transfer.**
  - This is the Jen–Kopra width-2 theorem in disguise: left-permutivity plays the rigidity, and the light-cone edge plays the growth ceiling.
  - Width 1 needs one more relation that pins a neighbouring column from c. Masked Jen (F1) supplies it only at black times.
- **Obstacle.**
  - One column does not determine the left half, because the right half is free. So there is no entropy deficit like log₂(3/2) < 1.
  - Rules 90, 150 and 210 share every ingredient (F-OR).
- **Artifacts.** CC0:
  - `RB/Rigidity.lean`, `RB/GeneralBase.lean`.
  - `ForMathlib/Combinatorics/SubwordComplexity.lean`, a finite Morse–Hedlund: complexity ≤ n on a window of length ≥ 3n forces a long periodic factor. This is useful for window certificates.

#### A6. Exact 2-adic arithmetic decoding (valuation traps, closed forms, linear forms in logarithms)
*Promise: low. Status: mixed, as listed under Proved.*
- **Origin.**

### B. Power series over F₂, linear complexity, automaticity

#### B1. Duhamel decomposition and Cartier closure of the 2-kernel
*Promise: medium. This is the only global route that passes the rule-90 firewall, and a long shot. Status: preprint; identity checked here for t ≤ 160.*
- **Origin.**
  - N. Berzai, [rule30-left-edge](https://github.com/nateberzai-svg/rule30-left-edge), Part II: paper of 2026-09-16, revised 09-24 and in October. "Computational and editorial assistance from Claude". MPL-2.0.
  - The same forcing identity appears in rule30-foundry's [CLAIM_LEDGER](https://github.com/Patto1155/rule30-foundry/blob/main/docs/CLAIM_LEDGER.md) (Codex and Claude agents) and in our archive's notes on the algebraic normal form.
- **Proved.**
  - U_{t+1} = ΛU_t + Q_t, with Λ = z + 1 + z⁻¹ (rule 150) and Q_t = Σ_x u_x·u_{x+1}·z^x (the quadratic source).
  - Hence c_t = 1 + Σ_{s<t} Σ_x T_{t−1−s}(x)·u^s_x·u^s_{x+1}, where T_m is the rule-150 propagator and T_m(0) = 1.
  - The class of such functionals is closed under the Cartier operators Λ₀ and Λ₁, because Λ(z)² = Λ(z²) in characteristic 2. So the 2-kernel of c is the image of an explicit orbit.
  - deg F_t = 2t − 1, with a unique top monomial.
  - Certified negatives: no Mahler relation of depth ≤ 12 and degree ≤ 8000; a census of ≥ 138,672 distinct truncations. The census route is provably closed.
- **Idea.** Rule 30 is rule 150 driven by the quadratic source, which is exactly the nonlinearity of the OR. Decimating by 2 maps the Duhamel class to itself, so non-automaticity is equivalent to the Cartier orbit being infinite.
- **Transfer.** Two routes:
  - find an invariant of the chiral Cartier recursion that takes infinitely many values; or
  - find an Allouche–Shallit–Yassawi family: one residue class per level, with pairwise distinct kernel elements.

  Either makes Σ c(t)xᵗ transcendental over F₂(x), and so proves Problem 1.
- **Obstacle.**
  - The target is strictly stronger than Problem 1: Thue–Morse is automatic and aperiodic.
  - No such invariant is known, and no finite census decides the question, since every finite word extends to an automatic sequence.
  - It passes F-OR by construction, because the source vanishes for linear rules. The local, strip and DFA barriers do not apply.
- **Artifacts.**
  - Berzai's paper (MPL-2.0).
  - Our identity check: `/Users/swish/.claude/jobs/b8cd2926/tmp/r30tech/portfolio/scripts/duhamel_check.py`.

### C. Factor complexity, words, per-word exclusion, and Problems 2–3

#### C1. Word-exclusion engines: a finite right strip, then (masked) Jen
*Promise: medium for partial results; none for periods 2–7. Status: preprint (Berzai, placego), partly reproduced; Lean (ours).*
- **Three implementations.**
  - **(a) Berzai's K-window interface automaton** (Part I; Claude-assisted; MPL-2.0). It excludes:
    - 1^b 0^a for b ≥ 9;
    - 1^b v for b ≥ 29 and |v| ≤ 12;
    - 0^m 11 for m = 6 and m ≥ 8;
    - words with isolated 1s and zero-runs ≥ 10;
    - 1 0^9; 1^7 0 (K = 10); 0^7 1 (K = 12);
    - necklaces whose cyclic zero-runs are all ≥ 19 (family certificate not re-checked).

    A boundary theorem says the method works exactly for words w whose interface language L(w) contains only eventually periodic members.
  - **(b) Strip graphs and stable sets.** Proposed in the agent-run [cochon123/rule30-prize](https://github.com/cochon123/rule30-prize), whose uniform Lemma F was wrong. Repaired in [placego PROOFS.md](https://github.com/ghywel/placego/blob/main/PROOFS.md) entries 38, 40 and 41 (GPT repair GC806; Claude re-implementation). It excludes:
    - 0 1^q for q = 7 or q ≥ 9;
    - 1 0^q for q ≥ 10;
    - 24 words of period 10–14 and 115 of period 15–18.

    Lean probes are in tests/probes/lean.
  - **(c) Our strip and rank certificates:** `Cert.sound` and `problem1_iff_no_word`, with 33 kernel-checked words of length 8–13 and about 180 more certified by two programs.
- **Verification.**
  - (a): our re-implementation confirmed that 1^8 0 is uncertified at K = 10, 00000011 is certified at K = 10, and 0^7 1 is certified at K = 12.

- **Idea.** Assume column 0 is eventually w^∞ and make the far right of the strip a free input. If every recurrent strongly connected component forces column 1 at the white letters of w to be eventually periodic, masked Jen finishes the proof.

#### D8. Barrier B7 (new): additive rankings cannot certify Q01
*Promise: none; it is a filter. Status: derived here, not machine-checked. It uses C6 (computed) and B2 (Lean).*
- **Statement.** Consider rankings of the form V(x) = Σ_d h(x_d, …, x_{d+r−1}) + B(wall window) + E(edge window) + a·width, with h of range r ≤ 8. No such V can be ≥ 0 and decrease by ≥ 1 on every surviving double step of the zero-driven left half. The same holds with piecewise-constant weights on finitely many regions anchored at the wall or the edge.
- **Proof sketch.**
  1. Whether a double step survives depends only on x₁…x₃. So any bulk word can sit between a surviving wall part and an edge part.
  2. The change of the bulk term is a sum of g over windows, where g is a local function on windows of length r + 4.
  3. A de Bruijn cycle of positive g-weight, pumped in the bulk, would make ΔV arbitrarily large. So no cycle is positive, and Bellman–Ford gives potentials ψ with g(e) ≤ ψ(head) − ψ(tail) on every edge.
  4. Rule 30² is surjective, so by Hedlund's theorem it maps the uniform measure on (r+4)-words to the uniform measure on r-words. The uniform circulation, which has full support, therefore has g-mean 0. Summing the slack ψ(head) − ψ(tail) − g ≥ 0 against it gives 0, so g = ψ(head) − ψ(tail) exactly.
  5. Then Σ h is conserved by rule 30² on finite configurations. By C6 every such law of range ≤ 8 is trivial, so V is a function of width, wall window and edge window. B2 (`no_local_ranking`) excludes that.
- **Two-sided version.** The same argument, with C6 for rule 30 (range ≤ 10) and `no_joint_local_ranking`, bars additive rankings that decrease at every flip of the centre, which is the CQ01 setting.
- **Not covered:**
  - max-plus rankings such as front positions (B6 already bars one max-type family);
  - lexicographic or k-step rankings, which would need C6 for rule 30^(2k);
  - arbitrary position weights;
  - rankings valid only on special subclasses, such as stripe-prefix families, where front arguments did work.
- **Explains** the archive's 15 failed monovariants.
- **Pitfall.** An LP restricted to rows of width ≤ W is always feasible, because V = C − width works at bounded width (Appendix B.6). A numeric test must encode the all-width conditions through de Bruijn potentials.

#### D11. Other busy-beaver-era and dynamics techniques

| Technique | Why it does not transfer |
|---|---|
| Arithmetisation of sporadic machines: BB(5) counters and Gray codes; LLM-written Rocq proofs for BB(6) (2 of 20 confirmed on 2026-08-15) | Needs exact macro rules. c(t) moves to a new diagonal every step. |
| Eventual-behaviour detection: translated cyclers, inductive rules, longitudinal acceleration | These prove that orbits become periodic. Skelet #1 starts cycling only after ~5.4×10⁵¹ steps, so finite absorption statistics are weak evidence either way. |
| Backward reasoning, halting segment | Backward trees never die: `barrier_exists`/`barrier_unique` and `column_realizable_unique`. |
| Cryptids (Antihydra, Hydra, Space Needle; BB(6) has 698 holdouts up to equivalence) | Same shape as our open statements, and no technique exists. "Probvious" heuristics have been wrong before. |
| Langton's ant ([arXiv 2409.10124](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.10124); Etse, MFCS 2026) | Non-repetition needs reversibility and a bounded domain. Rule 30 is irreversible, and the ZBL edge escapes. |
| Life SAT tools and Griddy ([arXiv 2305.01375](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01375)) | Answer finite existence questions only. |
| Aperiodic tilings (the hat; Greenfeld–Tao) | Whole-space aperiodicity would be false here: c7 and the stripe are infinite configurations with periodic centres. |
| Collatz cycle exclusion ([arXiv 2201.00406](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.00406)) | Needs an arithmetic constraint on the period, and none is known for rule 30. |

## 4. What not to repeat

### 4.1 Proof shapes our barrier theorems exclude

| Shape | Why it fails | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Finite-state certificates for Q01, CQ01, Absorption or short words: regular closed sets, n-gram/CPS/FAR, strip-SCC analyses, finite abstractions with rankings | Every finite abstraction has a reachable lasso along truncated stripes or c7 truncations. Strip graphs of words of length 2–7 contain SCCs whose white-phase outputs do not commute. | B1, B6, local obstruction, `word_lemma`; Berzai's boundary theorem; Stephan's Theorem D |
| Rankings through (width, wall window, edge window), and local two-sided rankings | Truncated stripes and c7 truncations | B2, JointBarrier |
| Additive potentials: pattern counts, potentials fitted by LP, BBB(4)-style counts, polynomial matrix interpretations | Over a random bulk the change has mean zero, which forces a conservation law, and none exists at range ≤ 8 | B7 (derived here), C6 |
| Ranking LPs over rows of bounded width | Vacuous: V = C − width always works | Appendix B.6 |
| Arguments using only left-permutivity, the light-cone edge, power-of-two diagonal periods, the odometer, Lucas or F₂-linearity, ANF degree, or dilation identities | They hold for rules 90, 150 and 210 (and, for the degree, LCP and rank variants, for rules 60, 22 and 126), whose centres are eventually periodic | F-OR; B5 controls |
| Left-only statements that ignore the finiteness of the right half | Q01-only witnesses; for rule 210 the left-only statement is false although period 2 is excluded | scope of B1/B2/B6; D5 |
| Edge structure plus windows shorter than the wall distance; backward reasoning; preimage trees | Every far part can be completed at will, and every column is realised | `edge_region_barrier`, `barrier_exists`/`unique`, `column_realizable_unique` |
| Finite windows, SAT bounds or a census offered as proofs of eventual statements | Finite rows fake periodic prefixes for about 1.25–1.9 times their radius; Condrey's H(2,w) ≥ w | F15, D10 |
| Zero-entropy interface exclusions (Sturmian, rotation, substitutive) used as the final step | The real interface has positive entropy | C2 |
| A single trap per word; low-complexity descriptions of the right half; simple monovariants | Refuted in rounds 1–2 | F3; write-up §8 |
| Extending strip-relaxation laws for period 2 | Superseded: the exact light-cone language implies them | Appendix B.2 |

### 4.2 Routes closed by the literature or by controls
- **Holonomic or analytic irrationality** on f = Σ c(t)zᵗ (Apéry, conservative matrix fields, G-functions, holonomy bounds, determinant methods): f is D-finite iff Problem 1 fails (A1).
- **Mahler, Adamczewski–Bugeaud and Subspace dichotomies:** they say nothing about the rational case (A9).
- **Liouville and tail decay on 0/1 digits:** the margin is zero (A3).
- **Measure-level, ergodic or mutual-information statements:** the single seed is invisible to them (Howe; Condrey's roundtable; Berzai).
- **Automatic-sequence, Walnut, number-wall or 2-kernel census certificates for c itself:** c needs ≥ 8,191 states, and every finite word extends to an automatic sequence.
- **Common errors in claimed proofs:**
  - Diagonal-period growth taken as evidence of aperiodicity; rule 90's Pascal diagonals grow too (Ulrey).
  - C(y)² = C(y²) misread as decimation (Topal).
  - Shortcut formulas for c: azhar's agrees with c 49.5% of the time; the c(t) = [t ∈ S_{t+1}] formula of arXiv 2604.00165 agrees 21/35.
  - Transferring the rule-210 clearing front to rule 30 (D5).
- **Counting-law measurements taken as a mechanism:** the law also holds for random centre words (D4).
- **Proxies that prove nothing about Problem 1:** density ½, a perfect LCP, maximal ANF degree, prediction rank, and Conjecture H (B5).
- **Square-free binary sequences (TLMC #1243):** impossible for length ≥ 4, and unrelated to Problem 1.

### 4.3 Process failures to avoid
- **Accepting an AI-written uniform step without an independent second reading:** cochon123's Lemma F; Shallit's v1 gap; Mantovanelli's v2 closure gap.
- **Trusting "solved" tags without auditing statement fidelity:** A6697, #5226, A379240, #263, and Aletheia's vacuous "correct" answers.
- **Lean trust:**
  - Do not trust Lean results without a replay: v4.30.0 predates the July 2026 kernel fixes.
  - Never use `native_decide`, `bv_decide` or metaprogrammed declarations.

  - Lean files can execute code during elaboration, so scan downloads before compiling them.

### 4.4 What a proof must look like (summary of the filters)
A proof must satisfy all of the following:
- use the OR;
- use the finiteness of the configuration in a way that no continuous (finite-memory or Cantor-continuous) reading can see;
- be non-local in space, and not additive at range ≤ 8;
- not rest on edge structure.

The candidate mechanisms that remain:
- an exact global description in special coordinates (Q-tilde style), though none has been found outside the boundary layers;
- an invariant of the Duhamel–Cartier orbit that takes infinitely many values;
- front-type (max-plus) quantities;
- counting arguments that exploit what is special about periodic centre words.

missing.name: Equivalent forms via other complexity measures: maximum-order (nonlinear) complexity and expansion complexity
missing.origin: Survey by Chunlei Li (Bergen). Z. Chen, Z. Chen, J. Obrovsky and A. Winterhof relate maximum-order and 2-adic complexity. Mérai, Niederreiter and Winterhof introduced expansion complexity (2017).
missing.proved:
Classical facts:
- A binary sequence is eventually periodic iff its N-th maximum-order complexity is bounded, because a bounded-order nonlinear feedback register is a finite-state map.
- By Christol and Mérai–Niederreiter–Winterhof, it is 2-automatic iff its expansion complexity is bounded.
- There are relations between maximum-order, 2-adic and linear complexity.
missing.core_idea: Maximum-order complexity is determined by the longest factor that occurs twice with different successors. Bounding it is exactly 'right-determinism at a fixed window', the same lemma behind Stephan's infinite Morse–Hedlund.
missing.transfer_to_rule30:
Two cheap library entries:
- Problem 1 iff the maximum-order complexity of c is unbounded. It follows from isEventuallyPeriodic_of_rightDeterministic in Stephan's CC0 InfiniteComplexity.lean.
- The non-automaticity strengthening iff the expansion complexity is unbounded.
Greenfeld–Moreira–Zelmanov (arXiv 2408.03403) show that any non-decreasing, submultiplicative function of at least linear growth is a subshift complexity. Complexity growth alone therefore cannot force more than Morse–Hedlund does.
missing.obstacle: These are equivalences only and restate the difficulty. The data on c (all length-44 windows distinct in 10^7 bits) say nothing asymptotic.
missing.artifacts: the survey; Stephan's CC0 Lean (InfiniteComplexity.lean, SubwordComplexity.lean) as the base for proofs

missing.proved: Termination and temporal-logic properties of software and hardware benchmarks, with machine-checked neural certificates.
missing.core_idea: Fit a ranking function (a network over the whole state) to sampled traces, then discharge 'decreases on every transition' with an exact solver. Counterexamples feed back into training (CEGIS).
missing.transfer_to_rule30: D7 and D8 leave open exactly the non-additive, global, max-plus and lexicographic certificate classes. B7 bars only additive rankings of range <=8, and B2 and JointBarrier bar only width plus bounded windows. Learned global rankings on ZBL or coupled rows are the natural AI search over that open space.
missing.obstacle: Solver checks cover only bounded widths, where the bounded-width pitfall applies (V=C-width trivially works). An all-width, parametric proof is still needed. Any ranking through a finite abstraction is barred by B1/B6 for Q01. It is missing from D7.
